definition_en: to fall or drop heavily and loosely, or to fail completely
core_image: 一袋湿沙从肩上滑落，平平地砸在地上摊成一团
scene: 新戏首演后评论冷淡，投资人脸色难看。The big-budget musical flopped after two weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 flopped 是「惨败」（第 5 个义项：彻底失败）；句意：这部大制作音乐剧上演两周后惨败。

pos.zh: 猛然落下；重重坐下；惨败
重摔；扑通声；失败之作；廉价旅馆

derivatives.zh: 由 flop 加词尾 -y 构成，义为「松软的；耷拉下来的」
由 flop 与 house 复合而成，义为「廉价旅馆」
由 floppy 加 -ness 构成，义为「松软；下垂」

senses.title: To fall heavily and loosely
senses.definition: to fall or drop suddenly with the whole weight of the body and no control
senses.definitionCN: 突然落下，整个重量砸下去，毫无控制
senses.example: The wet coat flopped onto the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 湿外套重重地掉在地板上。
senses.why: The word is probably an imitation of the dull sound of something heavy landing flat.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一般认为模仿重物平平落地的闷响，所以先有「重重摔下」的画面。

senses.title: To drop the body into a seat
senses.definition: to sit or lie down in a heavy, relaxed way, letting the whole body go
senses.definitionCN: 以沉重而放松的方式坐下或躺下，让整个身体松掉
senses.example: After the long walk he flopped into the nearest chair.
senses.exampleCN: 走了很远之后，他瘫进最近的椅子里。
senses.why: Once the sound names a fall, it easily names a person letting the body fall into a seat on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 声音先指「落下」，便很容易转指人主动把身体跌进座位。

senses.title: The thud of a landing
senses.definition: the dull sound made when something heavy and soft lands
senses.definitionCN: 沉重而柔软的东西落地时发出的闷响
senses.example: We heard a flop as the sack hit the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 口袋落地时，我们听到扑通一声。
senses.why: The noun keeps the sound itself, the part of the event that the ear remembers.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了声音本身，也就是这件事里耳朵记得住的那一部分。

senses.title: A public failure
senses.definition: a film, play, or product that fails badly with the public
senses.definitionCN: 在公众那里惨败的电影、戏剧或产品
senses.example: The expensive sequel was a flop.
senses.exampleCN: 那部昂贵的续集是失败之作。
senses.why: A failure lands flat, like a body that drops and does not get up, so the fall became a metaphor for defeat.
senses.whyCN: 失败像一具摔下后不再起来的身体，平平摊着，于是「摔落」成了「惨败」的比喻。

senses.title: To fail badly
senses.definition: to fail completely, especially after much money or hope has been spent
senses.definitionCN: 彻底失败，尤指投入了大量金钱或希望之后
senses.example: The new restaurant flopped within six months.
senses.exampleCN: 那家新餐厅半年内就惨败收场。
senses.why: The verb follows the noun: what lands flat has failed, and failing is the same fall.
senses.whyCN: 动词义跟着名词走：摔得平平的东西就是失败了，而失败这个过程也就是那次摔落。

senses.title: The first three shared cards in poker
senses.definition: the first three community cards placed face up on the table in poker
senses.definitionCN: 扑克牌局中最初摊在桌面上的三张公共牌
senses.example: She raised strongly after the flop.
senses.exampleCN: 翻牌之后她加注加得很凶。
senses.why: The cards are dealt in one quick spread, and players read the shape of the hand in that single drop.
senses.whyCN: 三张牌一次摊开，玩家在那一「摊」里就读出整手牌的轮廓，于是借用了这个词。

senses.title: A very cheap lodging house
senses.definition: a cheap house or hotel where people with little money can sleep
senses.definitionCN: 钱少的人可以过夜的廉价房屋或旅馆
senses.example: He found a flop house two streets from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他在离车站两条街的地方找到一家廉价旅馆。
senses.why: A tired body flops onto a bed, and the place that lets it do so took the name.
senses.whyCN: 疲惫的身体往床上一摊，收留这种「一摊」的地方也就得了这个名字。

intro.en: Flop is probably echoic, an English word shaped after the dull sound of a heavy body landing.
intro.cn: flop 一般认为属于拟声词，是照着沉重身体落地的闷响造出来的英语词。

items.en: The word appears in English in the eighteenth century, and no Latin or Germanic source is accepted.
items.cn: 这个词于十八世纪出现于英语；一般认为它没有可考的拉丁或日耳曼来源。

items.en: Flop is probably an imitation of the dull sound of a bundle or body landing flat.
items.cn: flop 很可能模仿包裹或身体平平落地的闷响。

items.en: The noun first names a heavy and awkward fall.
items.cn: 名词最初指沉重而笨拙的一摔。

items.en: The verb extends from things falling to a person dropping loose into a seat.
items.cn: 动词从物体落下扩展到人松散地跌进座位。

items.en: Theatre and film criticism give the word its sense of a failure.
items.cn: 戏剧与电影评论赋予这个词「失败」的含义。

items.en: Modern English adds the poker flop and the cheap lodging house.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上扑克翻牌与廉价旅馆两个义项。

note.en: First group holds near relatives and sound-alikes of flop; second group holds the ordinary English words for a failure.
note.cn: 第一组是 flop 的近亲与音近词；第二组是英语里表示「失败」的常用词。

normalIntro.en: Flop sounds like what it names: a soft heavy landing, then the flat silence that follows a failure.
normalIntro.cn: flop 的读音本身就像它指的事：沉重而柔软的一落，然后是失败之后平板的沉默。

normal.en: Flop down is the everyday phrase for dropping into a chair.
normal.cn: flop down 是「跌坐进椅子」的日常说法。

normal.en: A box-office flop loses money and reputation at once.
normal.cn: 「a box-office flop」既赔钱又赔名声。

normal.en: Floppy disks took their name from cases that hung loose and soft.
normal.cn: 软盘因外壳松软下垂而得名。

normal.en: The ending -y turns flop into floppy, meaning soft and hanging.
normal.cn: 词尾 -y 把 flop 变成 floppy，意为松软下垂的。

normal.en: Compare drop: a drop can be controlled, a flop never is.
normal.cn: 对比 drop：drop 可以是受控的，flop 从来不受控。

abstract.en: See a wet sandbag slide off a shoulder and hit the ground flat.
abstract.cn: 想象湿沙袋从肩上滑下，平平地砸在地上。

abstract.en: See a traveller let the whole body fall into a chair, arms hanging.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人把整个身体跌进椅子，双臂垂着。

abstract.en: Hear a dull thud with no bounce, the sound of a heavy thing landing.
abstract.cn: 听一声没有弹跳的闷响，那是重物落地的声音。

examples.en: The old sofa was so soft that you flopped into it.
examples.cn: 那张旧沙发太软，人一坐就陷进去。

examples.en: His first film was a flop, but the second one won awards.
examples.cn: 他的第一部电影惨败，第二部却得了奖。

examples.en: She flopped down on the grass and laughed.
examples.cn: 她一屁股倒在草地上笑了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛洛普」——听着像重物落地的一声闷响，扑通一下，事情也砸了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: flop 一般认为源自拟声，模仿重物落地的闷响，没有可考的拉丁词根；核心义是「松散而沉重地落下」，由此引申出「惨败」。

sensesIntro.en: Flop begins as a heavy loose fall and its sound, then names people sinking into seats, works that fail, and two specialised uses.
sensesIntro.cn: flop 从沉重松散的一落与那声闷响开始，再指人瘫进座位、作品惨败，最后是扑克与廉价旅馆两个专门用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet sandbag slipping off a shoulder and hitting the floor flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿沙袋从肩上滑落，平平地砸在地上。

branches.en: The physical fall of an object is the root sense.
branches.cn: 物体的重重落下是根本义项。

branches.en: A person dropping into a seat repeats the fall with a will.
branches.cn: 人跌进座位，是带着意愿重演那次落下。

branches.en: The sound of landing is the event as the ear keeps it.
branches.cn: 落地的那声闷响，是耳朵记住的事件版本。

branches.en: A failure is a fall that ends flat, as noun and as verb.
branches.cn: 失败就是一次摔到平平不起的落下，名词与动词两面都有。

branches.en: Poker cards and a cheap bed both borrow the single drop.
branches.cn: 扑克摊牌与廉价床位都借用了那一次「摊下」。

intro.en: Flop has no Latin root; English builds a small family around it with the adjective ending -y and with the compound flophouse.
intro.cn: flop 没有拉丁词根；英语围绕它加形容词词尾 -y 构成 floppy，并用复合方式构成 flophouse。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for flop, which is probably imitative, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: flop 没有可考的拉丁来源，一般认为它是拟声词，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Flop keeps the image of a body landing flat.
items.exampleCN: flop 保留身体平平落地的意象。

items.example: Flops is the present form used with one subject.
items.exampleCN: flops 是搭配单数主语的现在式形式。

items.example: Flopped describes a fall already finished.
items.exampleCN: flopped 描述已经结束的一摔。

items.example: Flopping keeps the fall in progress.
items.exampleCN: flopping 让那一下摔落保持在过程中。

items.example: The ending -y adds the quality of looseness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 添上「松散」的性质。

items.meaning: forming adjectives from nouns and verbs
items.meaningCN: 由名词或动词构成形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -y forms floppy from flop.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 由 flop 构成 floppy。

items.example: Flophouse joins flop and house in one word.
items.exampleCN: flophouse 把 flop 与 house 合成一个词。

items.meaning: the same lodging house written as two words
items.example: Flop house is the open spelling of the compound.
items.exampleCN: flop house 是这个词组的拆分拼写。

items.meaning: the quality of being soft and loose
items.example: The ending -ness names that quality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 为这种性质命名。

items.meaning: a heavy fall or a failure
items.example: The noun keeps both the fall and the failure.
items.exampleCN: 名词同时保留摔落与失败两层意思。

definition_zh: 花的；花卉图案的；花香的；花部的
definition_en: relating to flowers, or decorated with flowers or a flower pattern
core_image: 一只白瓷瓶里插满新摘的野花，花瓣落在桌布上
scene: 婚礼前一晚，礼堂换上成排的白花与新窗帘。The hall was decorated with floral curtains and white roses.
sceneCN: 这里 floral 是「花卉图案的」（第 2 个义项：以花卉图案装饰）；句意：大厅用印花窗帘和白玫瑰装饰。

pos.zh: 花的；花卉图案的；花香的；花部的
花卉图案布料；印花衣物

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 flor- 加 -ist 构成，义为「花商；花艺师」
由拉丁词干 flor- 与 culture 复合，义为「花卉栽培」
同出拉丁 flos，义为「过分华丽的；红润的」
同出拉丁 Flora，义为「（某地区的）植物群」

senses.title: Belonging to flowers
senses.definition: of or relating to flowers in general
senses.definitionCN: 泛指与花有关的
senses.example: The study compares floral colour across species.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究比较不同物种的花色。
senses.why: Flos is simply the Latin word for a flower, so the adjective begins as the plain label of flowers.
senses.whyCN: flos 本就是拉丁语「花」，所以这个形容词一开始只是给花贴的标签。

senses.title: Printed with flower designs
senses.definition: decorated with pictures of flowers rather than with real ones
senses.definitionCN: 用花朵图案而非真花装饰的
senses.example: She chose a floral wallpaper for the bedroom.
senses.exampleCN: 她给卧室选了花卉图案的壁纸。
senses.why: Cloth or paper printed with small flowers repeats the flower on a surface that holds no water, so the adjective moves from the plant to its picture.
senses.whyCN: 印着小花的布或纸，把花复刻在不吸水的表面上，于是这个词从「花」移到了「花的图像」。

senses.title: Smelling or tasting of flowers
senses.definition: having a scent or flavour that resembles flowers
senses.definitionCN: 气味或味道近似花朵的
senses.example: This white tea has a delicate floral aroma.
senses.exampleCN: 这款白茶有淡淡的花香。
senses.why: Perfume and wine borrow the adjective when their smell copies the flower without any flower being present.
senses.whyCN: 香水和葡萄酒在没有真花在场时借用了这个词，因为气味复制了花。

senses.title: Of the flower parts of a plant
senses.definition: relating to the reproductive structures of a flowering plant
senses.definitionCN: 指开花植物的生殖结构部分
senses.example: Botanists counted the floral organs under a lens.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家在放大镜下清点花部器官。
senses.why: Botany needs a precise adjective for the parts that make up a flower, and the general word narrows to fill that need.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要一个精确的词来指构成花的各部分，这个泛称便收窄了自己的范围。

senses.title: Flowers offered as a tribute
senses.definition: consisting of flowers given in memory of someone or in honour of someone
senses.definitionCN: 由花组成、用于悼念或致敬的
senses.example: A floral tribute lay across the coffin.
senses.exampleCN: 一副花圈横放在灵柩上。
senses.why: When flowers are arranged into one gift of mourning or honour, the adjective names the whole offering, not just the plants.
senses.whyCN: 当花被排成一份用于悼念或致敬的礼物时，这个词指整份献礼，而不只是植物。

senses.title: A flower-printed fabric
senses.definition: a fabric or garment printed with flowers, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 印有花卉图案的布料或衣物，作可数名词
senses.example: She picked a soft floral for the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她挑了一块柔软的印花布做夏装。
senses.why: Fashion drops the noun fabric and keeps the adjective, so a floral becomes the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 时尚业省掉了「布料」这个名词，只留下形容词，于是 floral 本身就变成了那件东西。

intro.en: Floral comes from Latin flos, a flower, whose stem floris supplies the whole family of floral, florist, and flora.
intro.cn: floral 来自拉丁语 flos（花），其词干 floris 撑起 floral、florist 与 flora 整个词族。

items.en: Flos means a flower, and its stem is floris.
items.cn: flos 意为花，其词干为 floris。

items.en: Floralis means belonging to flowers.
items.cn: floralis 意为属于花的。

items.en: Flora names the Roman goddess of flowers and spring.
items.cn: Flora 是罗马神话中的花与春天女神。

items.en: The adjective passes through French before it reaches English.
items.cn: 这个形容词经法语中转后才进入英语。

items.en: English takes floral as a learned adjective of flowers.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪把 floral 作为书卷气的「花的」形容词收入。

items.en: Modern English extends it to scents, wines, and printed fabrics.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到香气、葡萄酒与印花布料。

note.en: First group holds words grown from the same Latin stem; second group holds adjectives of flowers and plants that come from other roots.
note.cn: 第一组是从同一拉丁词干长出来的词；第二组是来自别的词根的「花」与「植物」形容词。

normalIntro.en: Floral is the adjective of the Latin flower: first a real bloom, later its picture, its smell, and its parts.
normalIntro.cn: floral 是拉丁语「花」的形容词：先是真花，后来是花的图案、花香与花部。

normal.en: Floral shares the stem flos with florist and floriculture.
normal.cn: floral 与 florist、floriculture 共用词干 flos。

normal.en: Floral curtains carry printed flowers, not real ones.
normal.cn: floral curtains 上印的是花，不是真花。

normal.en: A floral scent is the smell of flowers bottled in tea or wine.
normal.cn: a floral scent 是被装进茶或酒里的花香。

normal.en: Flora is the Roman goddess of flowers, and floral keeps her name alive.
normal.cn: Flora 是罗马的花神，floral 让她的名字延续下来。

normal.en: Compare flowery: flowery can also mean too ornate in speech.
normal.cn: 对比 flowery：flowery 还可以指言辞过分华丽。

abstract.en: Picture a white vase packed with freshly cut wild flowers.
abstract.cn: 想象一只白瓷瓶里插满刚剪下的野花。

abstract.en: Picture a cotton dress printed with tiny roses that never fade.
abstract.cn: 想象一条印着小玫瑰的棉布裙，那些花永不凋谢。

abstract.en: Imagine lifting a cup of jasmine tea and breathing in the steam.
abstract.cn: 想象端起一杯茉莉花茶，吸进升起的热气。

examples.en: The hotel lobby was filled with floral arrangements.
examples.cn: 酒店大堂摆满了插花作品。

examples.en: This tea has a light floral scent.
examples.cn: 这款茶有淡淡的花香。

examples.en: She wore a floral dress to the garden party.
examples.cn: 她穿着印花连衣裙去参加花园聚会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「芙洛拉」——听起来像花神的名字，满眼都是花；这只是谐音联想，与英语词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 flos（花，词干 floris）+ -alis（属于……的）→ 拉丁 floralis → 法语 floral → 英语 floral，核心义「与花有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Floral starts with flowers themselves, then moves to printed flowers, flower-like scent, the botanical flower parts, flower tributes, and finally floral fabric.
sensesIntro.cn: floral 从花本身出发，再指印出来的花、花香、植物学的花部、献花，最后指印花布料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white vase packed with freshly cut wild flowers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只白瓷瓶里插满刚剪下的野花。

branches.en: The plain relation to flowers is the base sense.
branches.cn: 与花的一般关系是基础义项。

branches.en: Printed flowers on cloth lead to the noun for the printed fabric itself.
branches.cn: 布上的印花通向指印花布料本身的名词用法。

branches.en: A scent that copies a flower is the smell sense.
branches.cn: 复制花香的气味构成「花香」义项。

branches.en: Botany narrows the word to the parts that make up a flower.
branches.cn: 植物学把词义收窄到构成花的各个部分。

branches.en: Flowers arranged as one gift become the tribute sense.
branches.cn: 花被排成一份礼物时，就成了「献花」义项。

intro.en: Floral is built on the Latin stem flor- with the adjective ending -alis, the same stem that yields florist, flora, and floriculture.
intro.cn: floral 由拉丁词干 flor- 加形容词词尾 -alis 构成；同一个词干还产出 florist、flora 与 floriculture。

latinIntro.en: Latin flos, stem floris, means a flower, and floralis means of flowers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flos（词干 floris）意为花，floralis 意为花的。

items.example: Flos is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: flos 是整个词族的词基。

items.example: Floris supplies the flor- seen in English.
items.exampleCN: floris 提供了英语里见到的 flor-。

items.example: Floralis is the direct model of floral.
items.exampleCN: floralis 是 floral 的直接原型。

items.example: The suffix -alis forms floralis from flos.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -alis 由 flos 构成 floralis。

items.example: The suffix -al shapes the English floral.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 塑成英语的 floral。

items.example: Floral keeps the Latin sense intact.
items.exampleCN: floral 完整保留了拉丁语的含义。

items.example: The ending -ist names the person who works with flowers.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 指与花打交道的从业者。

items.example: Floriculture joins the flower stem with culture.
items.exampleCN: floriculture 把「花」的词干与 culture 结合。

items.example: Flora keeps the name of the Roman flower goddess.
items.exampleCN: flora 保留了罗马花神的名字。

items.example: Florid adds the idea of abundance to flowers.
items.exampleCN: florid 在「花」上添了「繁盛」的意思。

definition_zh: 小舰队；小船队；一批小船
definition_en: a small fleet of boats or small ships, often sailing or working together
core_image: 清晨的港湾里，十几条小船并排解缆，像一群候鸟同时离岸
scene: 港口节庆那天，彩旗挂满堤岸，小船排队出海。A flotilla of small boats drifted past the harbour wall.
sceneCN: 这里 flotilla 是「小船队」（第 1 个义项：一起航行的一群小船）；句意：一支小船队漂过港口堤墙。

pos.zh: 小舰队；小船队；一批小船

derivatives.zh: flotilla 的复数形式，义为「多支小船队」
由 flotilla 与 leader 复合，义为「船队领舰；船队队长」
由 flotilla 与 commander 复合，义为「船队指挥官」

senses.title: A small fleet of boats
senses.definition: a group of small ships or boats sailing or working together
senses.definitionCN: 一起航行或作业的一群小船或小舰
senses.example: A flotilla of fishing boats left the bay at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 一支捕鱼船队在天亮时离开海湾。
senses.why: Flota already means a fleet, and the little ending -illa shrinks it to a modest group of ships.
senses.whyCN: flota 本已表示「船队」，指小词尾 -illa 又把它缩小成规模不大的一群船。

senses.title: A group of pleasure craft sailing together
senses.definition: a number of small boats that sail together for sport or leisure
senses.definitionCN: 为运动或休闲而结伴航行的一批小船
senses.example: The yacht club sent a flotilla across the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 游艇俱乐部派出一支船队横渡湖面。
senses.why: A club or a race needs a word for boats that travel as a friendly group, and a little fleet fits exactly.
senses.whyCN: 俱乐部或比赛需要一个词来指结伴同行的一群船，「小船队」正好合用。

senses.title: A naval formation of small warships
senses.definition: a unit of several small warships acting under one command
senses.definitionCN: 由若干小战舰组成、受同一指挥的单位
senses.example: The admiral ordered the flotilla to patrol the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 上将命令这支小舰队去海峡巡逻。
senses.why: Navies keep the word for a squadron of small warships that operate as one unit.
senses.whyCN: 海军沿用这个词，指作为一个单位行动的小型战舰编队。

senses.title: A group of vehicles moving together
senses.definition: a number of vehicles or craft travelling together like a small fleet
senses.definitionCN: 像小船队一样一起行进的一批车辆或飞行器
senses.example: A flotilla of taxis waited outside the station.
senses.exampleCN: 一队出租车等在车站外面。
senses.why: Once the word means a group moving as one on water, it stretches to any group of vehicles moving in company.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既然指水上一同行动的一群，便顺势扩展到任何结队行进的交通工具。

senses.title: A decorated fleet in a festival
senses.definition: a line of decorated boats taking part in a public celebration
senses.definitionCN: 参加公众庆典、装饰过的一列船
senses.example: The festival flotilla lit up the river.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆彩船队把河面照亮了。
senses.why: Celebrations gather boats into a parade, and the old word for a little fleet names the line of lights on the water.
senses.whyCN: 庆典把船聚成游行队列，这个表示「小船队」的老词便用来指水面上那一串灯火。

intro.en: Flotilla is Spanish, a diminutive of flota, a fleet that came to Spanish through Old French from a Germanic word for ships.
intro.cn: flotilla 来自西班牙语，是 flota（船队）的指小形式；flota 经古法语上溯到日耳曼语中表示船群的词。

items.en: A Germanic word for a company of ships lies behind the whole family.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「一群船」的词是整个词族的源头。

items.en: Flote names a fleet of ships in Old French.
items.cn: 古法语 flote 指船队。

items.en: Flota means a fleet in Spanish.
items.cn: 西班牙语 flota 意为船队。

items.en: The diminutive ending -illa turns flota into flotilla, a little fleet.
items.cn: 指小词尾 -illa 把 flota 变成 flotilla，即「小船队」。

items.en: English borrows flotilla for small squadrons at sea.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 flotilla，指海上的小型舰船编队。

items.en: Modern English loosens the word to almost any group of small craft.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义放宽到几乎任何一群小船。

note.en: First group holds the Spanish source, the floating root, and the naval compound; second group holds the larger fleet words.
note.cn: 第一组是西班牙语来源、漂浮词根与海军复合词；第二组是规模更大的「舰队」词。

entries.definition: the Spanish word for a fleet
entries.definitionCN: 西班牙语中表示「船队」的词，是 flotilla 的直接来源

entries.definition: to rest or move on the surface of water
entries.definitionCN: 漂浮；与 flotilla 同出日耳曼语「漂浮、船群」词根

entries.definition: the leading ship or officer of a small fleet
entries.definitionCN: 由 flotilla 与 leader 复合，指船队的领舰或队长

entries.definition: a group of ships sailing together
entries.definitionCN: 舰队；船队（规模通常大于 flotilla）

entries.definition: a large fleet of warships
a group of warships or aircraft under one command

normalIntro.en: Flotilla is a little fleet: Spanish flota plus the small ending -illa, so the word itself means a modest group of boats.
normalIntro.cn: flotilla 是「小船队」：西班牙语 flota 加指小词尾 -illa，词形本身就写着「规模不大的一群船」。

normal.en: Flotilla is Spanish flota plus the little ending -illa.
normal.cn: flotilla 是西班牙语 flota 加上指小词尾 -illa。

normal.en: A flotilla is smaller than a fleet: a handful of boats, not a navy.
normal.cn: flotilla 比 fleet 小：是几条船，而不是一整支海军。

normal.en: A naval flotilla patrols a strait as one unit.
normal.cn: a naval flotilla 作为一个单位在海峡巡逻。

normal.en: A festival flotilla lines the river with decorated boats.
normal.cn: 节庆彩船队用装饰过的船排满河面。

normal.en: Compare fleet: fleet is larger and more formal, flotilla is smaller and local.
normal.cn: 对比 fleet：fleet 更大更正式，flotilla 更小、更偏地方性。

abstract.en: Picture many small boats tied side by side, slipping out of harbour at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象许多小船并排系着，天亮时一起滑出港湾。

abstract.en: Picture kayaks moving across a lake in one loose line.
abstract.cn: 想象一群皮划艇排成松散的一线划过湖面。

abstract.en: Picture grey warships holding formation in a narrow strait.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色战舰在狭窄海峡里保持编队。

examples.en: A flotilla of fishing boats returned before the storm.
examples.cn: 一支捕鱼船队在暴风雨前返回了。

examples.en: The festival flotilla moved slowly down the river.
examples.cn: 节庆彩船队缓缓顺河而下。

examples.en: The navy sent a flotilla to guard the strait.
examples.cn: 海军派出一支小舰队去守卫海峡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「浮了提拉」——想象一群小船浮在水面，被缆绳一提拉成一排；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 西班牙语 flota（船队）+ 指小词尾 -illa → flotilla（小船队）；flota 又经古法语 flote 上溯日耳曼语，与 float（漂浮）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Flotilla names a small fleet, then a friendly group of pleasure boats, a naval squadron, a convoy of vehicles, and finally a decorated festival fleet.
sensesIntro.cn: flotilla 先指小船队，再指结伴出航的游艇、海军小舰队、结队行驶的车船，最后指节庆彩船队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dozen small boats casting off side by side at dawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：十几条小船在清晨并排解缆。

branches.en: The plain small fleet is the base sense.
branches.cn: 普通意义上的小船队是基础义项。

branches.en: Boats sailing for pleasure form the leisure sense.
branches.cn: 为休闲而结伴航行，构成游艇队义项。

branches.en: The same group under naval command becomes a squadron.
branches.cn: 同一群船置于海军指挥之下，就成为小舰队。

branches.en: The image of a group moving as one stretches to vehicles.
branches.cn: 「一群一同行进」的画面扩展到车辆。

branches.en: A celebration turns the group into a parade of lights.
branches.cn: 庆典把这一群船变成一串灯火游行。

intro.en: Flotilla is a Spanish diminutive, not an English prefix build: flota plus -illa, the ending that makes a thing small.
intro.cn: flotilla 是西班牙语的指小词，不是英语前缀构词：flota 加 -illa，这个词尾把事物变小。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for flotilla, whose line runs from Germanic through Old French into Spanish, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: flotilla 没有可考的拉丁来源，它的脉络从日耳曼语经古法语进入西班牙语，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Flota is the word flotilla is built from.
items.exampleCN: flota 是 flotilla 的构词基础。

items.example: The ending -illa makes the fleet a little one.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -illa 把船队变小。

items.example: Spanish flotilla already carries the small size.
items.exampleCN: 西班牙语 flotilla 已经带有「小」的意思。

items.example: English keeps the Spanish shape unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 英语原样保留了西班牙语的词形。

items.example: The plural adds -s to the borrowed word.
items.exampleCN: 复数只在这个外来词后加 -s。

items.meaning: the leading ship of a small fleet
items.example: Flotilla leader joins the noun to leader.
items.exampleCN: flotilla leader 把这个名词与 leader 结合。

items.meaning: the officer in charge of a flotilla
items.example: Flotilla commander names the officer in charge.
items.exampleCN: flotilla commander 指负责的军官。

items.meaning: to rest on the surface of water
items.example: Float shares the Germanic root of flota.
items.exampleCN: float 与 flota 共享日耳曼语词根。

items.example: Fleet is the larger English word for the same field.
items.exampleCN: fleet 是同一义场里规模更大的英语词。

items.example: Flotsam looks close but belongs to another branch.
items.exampleCN: flotsam 看似相近，却属于另一支派生词。

definition_zh: 挣扎；笨拙地行动；陷入困境；欧鲽
definition_en: to struggle helplessly in water or mud, or to act in a clumsy and confused way; also a flat sea fish
core_image: 一条鱼被冲上浅滩，身体拍打着泥沙却游不走
scene: 小船在浅水里翻了，他抓着船帮乱蹬。He floundered in the waist-deep water, unable to find the bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 flounder 是「在水中挣扎」（第 1 个义项：在水里乱蹬却站不稳）；句意：他在齐腰深的水里挣扎，踩不到底。

pos.zh: 挣扎；笨拙地移动；陷入困境
欧鲽（一种可食用的比目鱼）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「挣扎的；踉跄的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「挣扎；手足无措的状态」

senses.title: To struggle in water
senses.definition: to move the arms and legs with force but without control, especially in deep water or mud
senses.definitionCN: 在深水或泥里用力划动四肢却无法控制身体
senses.example: The swimmer floundered when the current pulled him down.
senses.exampleCN: 水流把他往下拖时，那名游泳者拼命挣扎。
senses.why: The word first pictures a body beating against water it cannot master.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘的是身体在无法驾驭的水里拍打。

senses.title: To move clumsily
senses.definition: to move or walk with clumsy, uneven effort
senses.definitionCN: 笨拙而吃力地移动或行走
senses.example: He floundered across the icy yard, arms wide for balance.
senses.exampleCN: 他张开双臂保持平衡，跌跌撞撞地穿过结冰的院子。
senses.why: From water the image spreads to any movement that lacks a steady footing.
senses.whyCN: 意象从水里扩展到任何踩不稳的移动。

senses.title: To be at a loss
senses.definition: to be in serious difficulty and not know how to act
senses.definitionCN: 身处严重困境而不知道该怎么行动
senses.example: The company floundered for months before it changed its plan.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在改变计划之前手忙脚乱了好几个月。
senses.why: A person who cannot find footing in water is the picture of being stuck.
senses.whyCN: 在水里找不到落脚点的人，正是陷入困境的形象。

senses.title: To speak with hesitation
senses.definition: to speak in a halting way, searching for words
senses.definitionCN: 说话断断续续，一边想一边找词
senses.example: Asked about the figures, she floundered for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 被问到那些数字时，她卡了一下，说不出话。
senses.why: Speech also needs footing, so when words will not come the tongue flounders.
senses.whyCN: 说话也需要落脚点，所以词句不来时舌头就像在乱蹬。

senses.title: The flatfish
senses.definition: a flat sea fish with both eyes on one side, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 一种两眼长在同一侧的可食用海鱼
senses.example: A flounder lay half buried in the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 一条欧鲽半埋在沙里。
senses.why: The fish name came into English separately, from the French name for this flat fish.
senses.whyCN: 鱼名是从法语中这类扁平海鱼的称呼单独进入英语的。

intro.en: Flounder has two stories: the verb of helpless struggling, whose origin is uncertain, and the fish name, which came through French.
intro.cn: flounder 有两条来路：表示无助挣扎的动词来源不确定，鱼名则经由法语传入。

items.en: Flounderen first means to stumble or struggle.
items.cn: flounderen 最初表示踉跄、挣扎。

items.en: Similar words mean to flop about, and may be the source.
items.cn: 荷兰语或低地德语中形近的词表示「扑腾」，可能是来源，但不确定。

items.en: The verb widens to any clumsy, helpless effort.
items.cn: 动词义扩大为任何笨拙而无助的努力。

items.en: Flondre names the flatfish.
items.cn: flondre 指这种扁平的海鱼。

items.en: A northern name for the same fish probably reinforced it.
items.cn: 北欧语言中同一鱼类的称呼很可能强化了这一用法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the fish and adds the sense of being at a loss.
items.cn: 现代英语保留鱼名，并增加「手足无措」的义项。

note.en: Flounder is a struggling verb with no certain root, next to spelling neighbours and to words for stumbling and thrashing.
note.cn: flounder 是一个词根不确定的「挣扎」动词，与几个拼写相近的词以及表示踉跄、乱动的词相邻。

entries.definition: to sink or fail completely
entries.definitionCN: 下沉；彻底失败（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to move with a sharp, impatient jerk
entries.definitionCN: 猛地一动；拂袖而去（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: struggling helplessly
entries.definitionCN: 无助挣扎的（由动词加 -ing 构成）

entries.definition: to try hard against difficulty
to lose balance while walking
to move about violently

normalIntro.en: Flounder is the body without footing, whether in water, on ice, or in the middle of a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: flounder 是没有落脚点的身体：在水里、在冰上，或在一句话说到一半时。

normal.en: Flounder about means to move or act in a clumsy, confused way.
normal.cn: flounder about 表示手忙脚乱地乱动。

normal.en: A swimmer who cannot touch the bottom flounders in the deep pool.
normal.cn: 在深水池里踩不到底的游泳者，就是在 flounder。

normal.en: To flounder for words is to search for the right phrase and fail.
normal.cn: flounder for words 就是找不到合适的说法。

normal.en: The fish called a flounder lies on the seabed with both eyes on one side.
normal.cn: 名叫 flounder 的鱼躺在海底，两只眼睛长在同一侧。

normal.en: Compare founder: to founder is to sink or fail, and it is a different word.
normal.cn: 对比 founder：founder 是沉没或失败，两者不是同一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a fish slapping the wet sand but never swimming away.
abstract.cn: 想象一条鱼拍打湿沙，却怎么也游不走。

abstract.en: Imagine boots slipping on ice while the arms wave for balance.
abstract.cn: 想象靴子在冰上打滑，双臂张开找平衡。

abstract.en: Think of a report with no clear next step and a team standing still.
abstract.cn: 想象一份报告没有写明下一步，整个团队都站在原地。

examples.en: The little boat floundered in the waves until the coast guard arrived.
examples.cn: 小船在浪里挣扎，直到海上救援队赶到。

examples.en: Without a clear plan, the project floundered for a whole year.
examples.cn: 没有清晰的计划，这个项目手忙脚乱地拖了整整一年。

examples.en: He floundered for words when the teacher asked him to explain.
examples.cn: 老师让他解释时，他结结巴巴地找不到词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「floun」听起来像「浮浪」，「der」像「打」——浮在浪上乱打，就是挣扎；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：中古英语 flounderen（踉跄、挣扎）可能来自荷兰语或低地德语中表示「扑腾」的词；鱼名另经古法语 flondre 传入，可能与北欧语同源。

sensesIntro.en: Flounder starts as a body beating against water, then widens to clumsy movement, to being at a loss, and to speech without footing; the fish is a separate name.
sensesIntro.cn: flounder 先指身体在无法驾驭的水里拍打，再扩展到笨拙的移动、手足无措，以及找不到词的说话；鱼名则是另一条来路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body beating against water it cannot master.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体在无法驾驭的水里拍打。

branches.en: Water is where the physical image begins.
branches.cn: 水里是这个意象的起点。

branches.en: The same lack of footing appears on land.
branches.cn: 同一种踩不稳的感觉出现在陆地上。

branches.en: Being stuck in a decision repeats the water picture.
branches.cn: 在决定上卡住，重复的正是水里的画面。

branches.en: Speech without words is another kind of floundering.
branches.cn: 说不出词的言语，是另一种挣扎。

branches.en: The flatfish is a separate name, not a branch of the verb.
branches.cn: 欧鲽是另一个来路的名称，并非动词意象的分支。

intro.en: Flounder has a small English family: the verb, its -ing forms, and the separate fish noun.
intro.cn: flounder 的词族不大：动词、它的 -ing 形式，以及单独的鱼名名词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin relative is known for the struggling verb; the fish name came through French, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 表示挣扎的动词没有已知的拉丁同族词；鱼名经法语传入，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Flounder is the core verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: flounder 是这个词族的核心动词。

items.example: The noun names a flat sea fish.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指一种扁平的海鱼。

items.example: Floundering describes an unsure movement.
items.exampleCN: floundering 形容没有把握的移动。

items.example: Floundering can name the struggle itself.
items.exampleCN: floundering 也可以指挣扎这件事。

items.example: Floundered is the past form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: floundered 是动词的过去式。

items.example: Flounders is the plural of the fish name.
items.exampleCN: flounders 是鱼名的复数。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或持续状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms floundering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 floundering。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms floundered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 floundered。

items.example: The suffix -er builds agent nouns.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成表示施动者的名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示复数或第三人称单数的词尾
items.example: The suffix -s forms flounders.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 flounders。

definition_zh: 流利；流畅；（技能）熟练自如
definition_en: the ability to speak or write a language easily and without long pauses, or the smooth quality of movement and skill
core_image: 河水贴着光滑的石面流过，没有一处被卡住
scene: 国际会议的台上，她连着讲了半小时几乎没有停顿。She answered every question with such fluency that the audience forgot she was working in a second language.
sceneCN: 这里 fluency 是「语言流利」（第 1 个义项：说外语轻松而准确）；句意：她回答每个问题都流利得让听众忘了她是在用第二语言发言。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 fluere（流动）加 -ent 构成，义为「流利的」
由 fluent 加 -ly 构成，义为「流利地」
与 fluency 同源，义为「流动的；流体的」

senses.title: Ease in a language
senses.definition: the ability to speak or write a language easily, accurately, and without long pauses
senses.definitionCN: 轻松、准确地使用一门语言而少有长时间停顿的能力
senses.example: Years of practice gave her real fluency in French.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的练习让她真正能流利地用法语。
senses.why: The Latin source means flowing, and speech that flows meets no block.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词源意为「流动」，流动的话语不会遇到阻塞。

senses.title: Smooth expression
senses.definition: the quality of speech or writing that moves smoothly from one idea to the next
senses.definitionCN: 口语或文章从一个意思顺畅过渡到下一个意思的品质
senses.example: The essay is admired for the fluency of its argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章因论证流畅而受到赞赏。
senses.why: Fluency moves from the mouth to the page, wherever words run without friction.
senses.whyCN: 流利从口头延伸到纸面，只要词句跑起来不带摩擦。

senses.title: Grace of movement
senses.definition: a smooth, unbroken quality in movement or performance
senses.definitionCN: 动作或表演中平滑而不中断的品质
senses.example: The dancer moved with the fluency of water.
senses.exampleCN: 那位舞者的动作像水一样流畅。
senses.why: Anything that flows without a break borrows the river image.
senses.whyCN: 任何不间断地流动的事物都借用了河流的意象。

senses.title: Skill that comes easily
senses.definition: ease and confidence in using a skill or a body of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 运用某项技能或知识时的轻松与自信
senses.example: Her fluency with numbers made the budget work simple.
senses.exampleCN: 她对数字的熟练让预算工作变得简单。
senses.why: Once a skill flows, effort stops showing, which is the last reach of the image.
senses.whyCN: 技能一旦流动起来，努力就不再显形，这是意象的最后一层延伸。

intro.en: Fluency comes from the Latin verb for flowing, and English first used it for speech that runs like water.
intro.cn: fluency 来自拉丁语中表示「流动」的动词，英语最早用它形容像水一样跑动的话语。

items.en: Fluere means to flow, like a river.
items.cn: fluere 意为流动，像河水一样。

items.en: Fluentia names a flowing.
items.cn: fluentia 指流动这一状态。

items.en: The participle fluens describes what is flowing.
items.cn: 分词 fluens 描述正在流动的东西。

items.en: Fluency appears in English as smooth, flowing speech.
items.cn: 一般认为 fluency 在十七世纪进入英语，指顺畅流动的言语。

items.en: The word extends from speech to writing and style.
items.cn: 这个词从口语扩展到文章与文风。

items.en: Modern use adds movement, skill, and language tests.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了动作、技能与语言测试的含义。

note.en: Fluency belongs to the Latin flowing family of fluent, fluid, and influx, and it is close to words for ease and eloquence.
note.cn: fluency 属于拉丁语「流动」词族，与 fluent、fluid、influx 同根，并与表示轻松、雄辩的词相邻。

entries.definition: able to speak a language easily
entries.definitionCN: 流利的（与 fluency 同出拉丁语 fluere）

entries.definition: able to flow; a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 流动的；流体（与 fluency 同出拉丁语 fluere）

entries.definition: a flowing in of people or things
entries.definitionCN: 涌入；流入（拉丁语 in- 加 fluere）

entries.definition: a high level of skill in something
entries.definitionCN: 熟练；精通（强调技能水平而非顺畅感）

entries.definition: the power to speak well and move people
entries.definitionCN: 雄辩；口才（强调感染力而非顺畅）

entries.definition: the quality of being even and without bumps
entries.definitionCN: 平滑；顺畅（可用于动作与文句）

normalIntro.en: Fluency is the river in speech: nothing blocks it, so the words keep moving.
normalIntro.cn: fluency 是言语里的河流：没有东西拦着，词句就一直往前走。

normal.en: Fluency and fluent share the Latin river, because both describe what flows.
normal.cn: fluency 与 fluent 共享拉丁语「河流」的词根，两者都形容流动的东西。

normal.en: The phrase speak with fluency is the usual pattern for the noun.
normal.cn: speak with fluency 是这个名词最常用的搭配。

normal.en: Fluency in a language is judged by ease, not by speed alone.
normal.cn: 判断一门语言的流利度看的是轻松，而不只是速度。

normal.en: Compare fluid: fluid is what can flow, fluency is how well words flow.
normal.cn: 对比 fluid：fluid 指能流动的东西，fluency 指词句流动得好不好。

normal.en: The suffix -ency turns the adjective fluent into the noun fluency.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ency 把形容词 fluent 变成名词 fluency。

abstract.en: Picture a river sliding over smooth stones without a single pause.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河贴着光滑的石头流下，一次也不停顿。

abstract.en: Imagine a reader moving down a page and never stumbling on a sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者一路读下去，从不在某个句子上绊住。

abstract.en: Think of a dancer whose turns never break the line of motion.
abstract.cn: 想象一位舞者转身时，动作的线条从不断开。

examples.en: She speaks English with remarkable fluency for someone who began at twenty.
examples.cn: 对一个二十岁才开始学的人来说，她的英语说得流利得惊人。

examples.en: The fluency of the dialogue makes the film easy to follow.
examples.cn: 对白的流畅让这部电影很容易看懂。

examples.en: Daily reading builds fluency faster than memorising word lists.
examples.cn: 每天阅读比背单词表更快地培养流利度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「flu」听起来像「浮流」——话像浮在水上的叶子，顺流而下不停顿，就是流利；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 fluere（流动）→ 拉丁语 fluentia（流动）→ 英语 fluent（流动的、流利的）→ fluency（流利），核心义「像水一样顺畅不停」。

sensesIntro.en: Fluency begins with a language that flows, then covers smooth writing, unbroken movement, and finally any skill that looks effortless.
sensesIntro.cn: fluency 从流动的语言开始，再指顺畅的文章、不间断的动作，最后指任何看起来毫不费力的技能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river sliding over smooth stones with nothing blocking it.
core.cn: 核心意象：河水贴着光滑的石头流过，没有什么拦住它。

branches.en: A flowing language is the first and most common sense.
branches.cn: 流动的语言是最早也最常见的义项。

branches.en: The same current carries over from mouth to page.
branches.cn: 同一股水流从口头延续到纸面。

branches.en: Movement borrows the river when it never breaks.
branches.cn: 动作只要从不断开，就借用了河流的意象。

branches.en: A skill that flows hides its effort.
branches.cn: 流动起来的技能会把努力藏起来。

branches.en: Both speech and writing are judged by how little they stumble.
branches.cn: 口语与文章都按「卡顿多少」来评判。

intro.en: Fluency belongs to the Latin fluere family, which flows into fluent, fluid, influx, and confluence.
intro.cn: fluency 属于拉丁语 fluere 词族，这个词族流向 fluent、fluid、influx 与 confluence。

latinIntro.en: Latin fluere means to flow, fluentia means a flowing, and the participle fluens gives the adjective fluent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fluere 意为流动，fluentia 意为流动，分词 fluens 给出形容词 fluent。

items.example: Fluere is the river behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: fluere 是整个词族背后的那条河。

items.example: Fluentia is the direct noun source.
items.exampleCN: fluentia 是名词的直接来源。

items.example: Fluens feeds the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: fluens 提供了英语形容词的词形。

items.example: Fluent describes a speaker who does not pause.
items.exampleCN: fluent 形容说话不卡顿的人。

items.example: The adverb -ly marks the manner.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾 -ly 标记方式。

items.example: Fluency names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: fluency 指这种性质本身。

items.example: Fluid keeps the physical flow sense.
items.exampleCN: fluid 保留具体的流动含义。

items.example: The prefix in- adds the direction inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 增加了向内的方向。

items.example: The prefix con- adds together.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 增加了「共同」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ency forms fluency from fluent.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ency 把 fluent 变成 fluency。

definition_zh: 长笛；笛状凹槽；吹长笛
definition_en: a long, thin musical instrument that you blow, or something shaped like it, such as a groove in stone or a tall glass
core_image: 一根细长的银管贴在下唇，气流穿过，流出清亮的音
scene: 音乐教室里，女孩把银色的小管凑到唇边。The girl raised the flute to her lips and held a long, clear note.
sceneCN: 这里 flute 是「长笛」（第 1 个义项：一种吹奏乐器）；句意：女孩把长笛举到唇边，吹出一个悠长的清音。

pos.zh: 长笛；笛状凹槽；细长高脚杯

derivatives.zh: 由 flute 加 -ist 构成，义为「长笛手」
由 flute 加 -ed 构成，义为「带竖凹槽的；笛形的」
由 flute 加 -ing 构成，义为「凹槽；吹笛」

senses.title: The instrument
senses.definition: a long, thin tube with holes or keys that is played by blowing air through it
senses.definitionCN: 一种细长、带孔或按键、靠吹气发声的管乐器
senses.example: She has played the flute since she was nine.
senses.exampleCN: 她九岁起就吹长笛。
senses.why: The name came from the act of blowing, so the instrument is named for the breath that fills it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自「吹」的动作，乐器因灌入其中的气息而得名。

senses.title: A vertical groove
senses.definition: one of the shallow vertical channels cut into a column or a piece of wood
senses.definitionCN: 柱子或木料上凿出的浅竖槽
senses.example: Each flute on the column catches a thin line of shadow.
senses.exampleCN: 柱子上的每道凹槽都投下一条细影。
senses.why: A cut channel looks like a long tube opened along its length.
senses.whyCN: 凿出的长槽看上去像沿长度剖开的长管。

senses.title: To play the flute
senses.definition: to play a flute, or to produce flute-like notes
senses.definitionCN: 吹奏长笛，或发出笛子般的音
senses.example: A boy fluted a tune in the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 一个男孩在走廊里用笛子吹出一支曲子。
senses.why: The instrument name turns into a verb for the act it performs.
senses.whyCN: 乐器名转化为动词，指它所发出的那个动作。

senses.title: A flutelike voice
senses.definition: a high, clear, breathy singing or speaking voice
senses.definitionCN: 高而清亮、带气息感的歌声或说话声
senses.example: Her voice fluted over the choir like a solo bird.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音像一只独唱的鸟，在合唱上方清亮地飘起。
senses.why: The thin, airy tone of the instrument is borrowed for the human voice.
senses.whyCN: 乐器那种细薄而带气息的音色被借来形容人声。

senses.title: The tall glass
senses.definition: a tall, narrow glass used for sparkling wine
senses.definitionCN: 一种细长、用于起泡酒的高脚杯
senses.example: He poured the wine into a flute and watched the bubbles rise.
senses.exampleCN: 他把酒倒进笛形杯，看着气泡升起来。
senses.why: The slender outline repeats the shape of the instrument in glass.
senses.whyCN: 细长的轮廓把乐器的形状复制到了玻璃上。

intro.en: Flute reached English through French from a word for blowing, and the same Latin root gives flatus and inflate.
intro.cn: flute 经法语进入英语，源头是一个表示「吹」的词，同一拉丁词根还给出 flatus 与 inflate。

items.en: Flare means to blow or breathe out.
items.cn: flare 意为吹气、呼气。

items.en: Flatus names a blowing or a blast of air.
items.cn: flatus 指吹气或一阵气流。

items.en: Flauta is the pipe name in the south of France.
items.cn: flauta 是法国南部对这种管笛的称呼。

items.en: Flaute carries the instrument name north.
items.cn: flaute 把这个乐器名带到北方。

items.en: Floute appears in English for a pipe or a whistle.
items.cn: floute 在英语中指点笛或哨管。

items.en: Modern English adds grooves, tall glasses, and flute-like voices.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了凹槽、细长酒杯与笛声般的嗓音。

note.en: Flute has a small family of its own in flutist, fluted, and fluting, and it sits beside other wind instruments.
note.cn: flute 自己有 flutist、fluted、fluting 这个小词族，并与其它吹奏乐器相邻。

entries.definition: a person who plays the flute
entries.definitionCN: 长笛手（由 flute 加 -ist 构成）

entries.definition: having vertical grooves, or shaped like a flute
entries.definitionCN: 带竖凹槽的；笛形的（由 flute 加 -ed 构成）

entries.definition: the grooves on a column, or the act of playing a flute
entries.definitionCN: 柱子上的凹槽；吹笛（由 flute 加 -ing 构成）

entries.definition: a straight wind instrument with a wooden or plastic tube
entries.definitionCN: 竖笛；八孔直笛（与长笛同属吹奏乐器）

entries.definition: a wooden wind instrument with a curved body
entries.definitionCN: 单簧管；黑管（与长笛同属管乐器）

entries.definition: a simple tube used to make music
entries.definitionCN: 笛；管乐器（泛指简单管状吹奏器）

normalIntro.en: Flute is breath turned into a clear tone by a long, hollow tube.
normalIntro.cn: flute 是气息被一根细长空心管变成清亮音调的东西。

normal.en: A flute is played by blowing air through a long tube.
normal.cn: 吹长笛就是把气送进一根细长的管子里。

normal.en: The player is a flutist, and fluted describes a grooved surface.
normal.cn: 吹奏者叫 flutist，fluted 则形容带凹槽的表面。

normal.en: A champagne flute borrows the tall, narrow outline of the instrument.
normal.cn: 香槟笛杯借用了乐器细长的轮廓。

normal.en: Classical columns are decorated with flutes cut into the stone.
normal.cn: 古典柱子上雕有凿进石料的竖凹槽。

normal.en: Compare recorder and clarinet: all are wind instruments, but only one is a flute.
normal.cn: 对比 recorder 与 clarinet：它们都是管乐器，但只有一个是长笛。

abstract.en: Picture a silver tube held to the lips, with one clear note rising.
abstract.cn: 想象一根银管贴在唇边，一个清亮的音升起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a column cut with long vertical channels like split tubes.
abstract.cn: 想象一根柱子被凿出长长的竖槽，像剖开的管子。

abstract.en: Think of a tune so thin and airy that it seems made of breath.
abstract.cn: 想象一支细薄轻飘的曲子，仿佛是用气息织成的。

examples.en: The orchestra flutist tuned her flute before the concert began.
examples.cn: 管弦乐团的长笛手在音乐会开始前给长笛调音。

examples.en: Old stone columns were fluted to catch the changing light.
examples.cn: 古老的石柱被凿出竖槽，以承接变化的光线。

examples.en: A flute of cold champagne stood on the silver tray.
examples.cn: 银托盘上放着一杯冰香槟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「flute」听成「浮芦特」——一根芦苇管，吹气就响，声音又细又清；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 古法语 flaute（管笛）与普罗旺斯语 flauta 传入英语；一般认为可追到拉丁语 flare（吹气），与 flatus（一阵气）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Flute starts as the blowing instrument, then lends its shape to grooves and tall glasses, and its sound to voices and to a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: flute 从吹奏的乐器开始，再把形状借给凹槽与细长酒杯，把声音借给人声，并转化为动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long, thin tube that turns breath into a clear tone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细长的管子把气息变成清亮的音。

branches.en: The instrument is the source of the whole family.
branches.cn: 乐器是整个词族的源头。

branches.en: A groove copies the long channel of the tube.
branches.cn: 凹槽复制了管子的长通道形状。

branches.en: The noun becomes a verb for the playing itself.
branches.cn: 名词转化为动词，指吹奏这个动作。

branches.en: A thin, airy voice borrows the tone of the instrument.
branches.cn: 细薄轻飘的嗓音借用了乐器的音色。

branches.en: The tall glass repeats the slender outline.
branches.cn: 细长酒杯重复了那种纤细的轮廓。

intro.en: Flute has a small English family built on the instrument: flutist, fluted, fluting, and the verb flute.
intro.cn: flute 有一个围绕乐器形成的小词族：flutist、fluted、fluting，以及动词 flute。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare, to blow, and flatus, a blast of air, stand behind the French name of the instrument.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flare（吹气）与 flatus（一阵气流）是这个乐器法语名称背后的来源。

items.example: The noun names the instrument.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指乐器本身。

items.example: The verb names the playing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指吹奏的动作。

items.example: Flutes is the plural form.
items.exampleCN: flutes 是复数形式。

items.example: The suffix -ist marks the player.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 标记演奏者。

items.example: Fluted describes carved stone.
items.exampleCN: fluted 形容雕出凹槽的石头。

items.example: Fluting keeps both the shape and the sound.
items.exampleCN: fluting 同时保留形状与声音两层意思。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms flutist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 flutist。

items.meaningCN: 表示「具有……性质的」形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms fluted.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 fluted。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms fluting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 fluting。

items.example: Flare is the oldest member of the group.
items.exampleCN: flare 是这一组里最古老的成员。

items.example: Flatus keeps the sense of moving air.
items.exampleCN: flatus 保留「流动的空气」这一含义。

items.example: Flaute brings the name into English.
items.exampleCN: flaute 把这个名称带进英语。

definition_zh: 振翅；拍翅；飘动；心怦怦跳；紧张不安
definition_en: to move the wings or body with quick light beats, or to move lightly and unevenly in the air
core_image: 蝴蝶翅膀贴着草尖又快又轻地扇动
scene: 黄昏的草丛里，一只白蝴蝶贴着草尖上下扇动翅膀。At dusk, a white butterfly fluttered above the grass tips without settling.
sceneCN: 这里 flutter 是「振翅、拍翅」（第 1 个义项：鸟或昆虫快速而轻地扇动翅膀）；句意：黄昏的草丛里，一只白蝴蝶贴着草尖上下扇动翅膀。

derivatives.zh: 由 a-（处于某种状态）+ flutter 构成，义为「飘动的；心慌的」，多作表语
flutter + -y 构成形容词，义为「轻飘的；心神不定的」
flutter + -ing 转成名词，义为「振翅；飘动；扑动声」

senses.title: To beat the wings quickly and lightly
senses.definition: of a bird, insect, or bat, to move the wings in quick light beats
senses.definitionCN: 指鸟、昆虫或蝙蝠快速而轻地扇动翅膀
senses.example: A moth fluttered against the lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蛾子扑着灯罩扇翅。
senses.why: The core image is a pair of wings striking the air in short rapid beats, and this is the oldest recorded sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一对翅膀以短促快速的节拍拍打空气，这也是最早记录的义项。

senses.title: To drift or wave in the air
senses.definition: to move lightly and unevenly through the air, or to wave gently in a current of air
senses.definitionCN: 轻而不稳地飘过空中，或在气流里轻轻摆动
senses.example: The flag fluttered above the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 旗子在门楼上飘动。
senses.why: Once the rapid beat is seen in flags, paper, and leaves, the word names any light object that stirs in the air.
senses.whyCN: 当这种快速拍动被看到在旗子、纸张和树叶上发生时，词义就扩展到任何在空气里轻晃的轻物。

senses.title: To beat fast and irregularly
senses.definition: of the heart, to beat quickly and unevenly because of excitement or fear
senses.definitionCN: 指心脏因兴奋或恐惧而快速而不规则地跳动
senses.example: Her heart fluttered when the letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 信到的时候，她的心怦怦直跳。
senses.why: A heartbeat that skips and races feels like a wing beating inside the chest, so the image moves inward.
senses.whyCN: 心跳快而不齐时，感觉就像胸腔里有一只翅膀在拍打，意象由此转向身体内部。

senses.title: A state of nervous excitement
senses.definition: a state of restless excitement or mild agitation
senses.definitionCN: 一种坐立不安的兴奋或轻微慌乱状态
senses.example: The whole office was in a flutter before the visit.
senses.exampleCN: 来访之前，整个办公室都人心浮动。
senses.why: When many hearts flutter at once, the feeling becomes a shared atmosphere, and the noun names that state.
senses.whyCN: 当许多颗心同时怦怦跳时，这种感觉变成共同的气氛，名词就用来指这种状态。

senses.title: A small bet
senses.definition: a small, casual bet, especially on a horse race
senses.definitionCN: 尤指赛马时下的金额不大、带消遣性质的赌注
senses.example: He likes a flutter on the horses on Saturdays.
senses.exampleCN: 他星期六喜欢在赛马上下点小注。
senses.why: The thrill of a small bet is a light flutter of excitement, so British English borrows the noun for the wager itself.
senses.whyCN: 小赌带来的刺激正是一种轻微的兴奋「扑动」，英式英语便用这个名词来指赌注本身。

senses.title: A rapid abnormal heart rhythm
senses.definition: a very fast, irregular rhythm of the heart, as in atrial flutter
senses.definitionCN: 心脏非常快速而不规则的一种节律，如心房扑动
senses.example: The monitor showed atrial flutter during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间监护仪显示出了心房扑动。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the literal image of a flapping beat and gives it a precise name for a disordered rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了「拍打式跳动」的字面意象，用它精确命名一种节律紊乱。

intro.en: Flutter is first recorded in the sixteenth century for quick irregular flapping, and its deeper origin is uncertain and usually called imitative.
intro.cn: flutter 于十六世纪首次被记录，指快速而不规则的拍动；更早的来源不确定，通常被认为是拟声词。

items.en: A Germanic base for flapping or floating is usually reconstructed behind the word, but its exact form is not settled.
items.cn: 一般认为，这个词背后有一个表示「拍打、漂浮」的日耳曼语词根，但确切形式尚无定论。

items.en: Middle Dutch flodderen, to flap or flop about, is the closest recorded relative.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 flodderen（扑动、晃荡）是记录中最接近的亲属。

items.en: Flutter enters English as a name for quick, light, irregular wing beats.
items.cn: flutter 进入英语时，指快速、轻而不规则的振翅。

items.en: The verb widens to flags, paper, and the heart, all moving in short light beats.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，动词用法扩展到旗子、纸张与心脏，都是短促轻快的跳动。

items.en: Modern use adds nervous excitement, a small bet, and the medical rhythm called flutter.
items.cn: 现代用法又增加了紧张兴奋、小额赌注，以及医学上的「扑动」心律。

note.en: Flutter sits beside sound-alike motion verbs, its own derived adjectives, and the plainer words for trembling.
note.cn: flutter 与读音相近的动作动词、自身派生的形容词，以及更朴素的「颤动」类词相邻。

entries.definition: moving lightly, or nervously excited
entries.definitionCN: 飘动的；心慌的（由 a- 加 flutter 构成）

entries.definition: to move quickly and lightly from place to place
entries.definitionCN: 轻快地掠过；与 flutter 只是拼写和读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make someone nervous and confused
entries.definitionCN: 使慌乱；与 flutter 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to move a wing or a flat object up and down
entries.definitionCN: 上下拍打翅膀或扁平物

entries.definition: to shake with a slight rapid movement
to shake slightly, often from fear or cold
entries.definitionCN: 因恐惧或寒冷而轻轻发抖

normalIntro.en: Flutter is the sound and shape of a light wing beat, repeated until it becomes a flag, a heartbeat, or a room full of nerves.
normalIntro.cn: flutter 是轻翅一拍的声音与形状，反复出现，直到变成旗子、心跳，或一屋子紧张的人。

normal.en: Flutter and flit both suggest light, quick movement, but flutter keeps a flapping beat.
normal.cn: flutter 与 flit 都表示轻快的移动，但 flutter 保留「一下一下拍打」的节拍。

normal.en: A flag flutters in the wind; a bird flutters its wings. Both are short light beats.
normal.cn: 旗子在风里 flutter，鸟在「flutter its wings」，两者都是短促轻巧的拍动。

normal.en: When the heart flutters, the beat feels like a wing inside the chest.
normal.cn: 「heart flutters」时，心跳就像胸腔里有一只翅膀。

normal.en: In a flutter means nervous and excited, like a room just before important news.
normal.cn: 「in a flutter」指紧张又兴奋，像消息公布前的房间气氛。

normal.en: Have a flutter is British for a small bet, a light risk rather than a heavy one.
normal.cn: 「have a flutter」是英式说法，指小赌一把，风险很轻。

abstract.en: Picture a butterfly whose wings tap the air twice every second.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蝴蝶，翅膀每秒在空气里轻拍两下。

abstract.en: Picture a thin flag snapping and softening in a gust.
abstract.cn: 想象一面薄旗在阵风里忽紧忽松地抖动。

abstract.en: Picture a small wing beating behind the ribs when news arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象消息到来时，肋骨后面有一只小翅膀在扑打。

examples.en: A pigeon fluttered down onto the window ledge.
examples.cn: 一只鸽子扑扇着落到窗台上。

examples.en: The pages fluttered in the draft from the open door.
examples.cn: 书页被敞开的门带来的气流吹得轻轻翻动。

examples.en: She felt a flutter of anxiety before the interview.
examples.cn: 面试前她感到一阵不安的悸动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「flutter」读起来像「弗拉特」，一串轻飘飘的扑啦声，翅膀一扇就过去了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自日耳曼语中表示「拍打、漂浮」的拟声词根，与中古荷兰语 flodderen（扑动）、低地德语 fluttern 同源；英语中十六世纪始见，核心义为「轻而快地拍动、飘动」。

sensesIntro.en: Flutter starts with the quick light beat of wings, passes to anything drifting in air, moves inward to the heart, then to shared nervous excitement, a small bet, and finally a named abnormal rhythm.
sensesIntro.cn: flutter 从翅膀轻快的拍动出发，转到在空中飘动的轻物，再转向心跳，进而指共同的紧张兴奋、小额赌注，最后成为异常心律的专业名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of wings beating fast and light against the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一对翅膀在空气里又快又轻地拍打。

branches.en: The literal wing beat is the root sense.
branches.cn: 字面上的振翅是词义的根。

branches.en: The same beat appears in flags and paper, which drift instead of flying.
branches.cn: 同样的拍动出现在旗子和纸上，它们不飞而是在飘。

branches.en: The beat turns inward when the heart copies the rhythm of a wing.
branches.cn: 当心脏模仿翅膀的节律时，拍动转向了身体内部。

branches.en: A room of fluttering hearts becomes a named mood of nervous excitement.
branches.cn: 一屋子怦怦跳的心，汇成一个有名字的紧张兴奋状态。

branches.en: Two specialized extensions take the quick irregular beat into gambling and medicine.
branches.cn: 两个专门化延伸把这种快速不规则的跳动带入赌博与医学。

intro.en: Flutter is a Germanic verb with a small English family built from suffixes and the a- prefix.
intro.cn: flutter 是日耳曼语来源的动词，英语中用后缀与 a- 前缀构成了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Flutter has no Latin root; it belongs to the Germanic and imitative layer of English vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: flutter 没有拉丁语词根，属于英语词汇里日耳曼语与拟声的那一层。

items.example: Birds flutter when they hover.
items.exampleCN: 鸟悬停时会轻轻振翅。

items.meaningCN: flutter 的第三人称单数形式
items.example: The flag flutters all day.
items.exampleCN: 旗子整天飘动。

items.example: The leaves fluttered down.
items.exampleCN: 树叶飘落下来。

items.example: A fluttering curtain woke her.
items.exampleCN: 飘动的窗帘把她弄醒了。

items.example: The suffix -y turns flutter into fluttery.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 flutter 变成 fluttery。

items.example: Her voice sounded fluttery.
items.exampleCN: 她的声音听起来有点发飘。

items.example: The prefix a- forms aflutter.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 a- 构成 aflutter。

items.example: The curtains were aflutter.
items.exampleCN: 窗帘在轻轻飘动。

items.example: Moths flit around the lamp.
items.exampleCN: 蛾子在灯边轻快地飞。

definition_zh: 泡沫；起泡沫；泡沫材料
definition_en: a mass of small bubbles on the surface of a liquid, or to produce such a mass
core_image: 啤酒杯口那层细密的白泡
scene: 海浪拍上礁石，退下去时在石缝里留下一层白白的泡沫。Waves hit the rocks and left a band of foam behind as they withdrew.
sceneCN: 这里 foam 是「泡沫」（第 1 个义项：液体表面聚集的细小气泡）；句意：海浪拍上礁石，退下去时在石缝里留下一层白白的泡沫。

derivatives.zh: foam + -y 构成形容词，义为「起泡沫的；泡沫状的」
foam + -less 构成形容词，义为「没有泡沫的」
foam + -ing 作形容词，义为「起泡的；泛着白沫的」

senses.title: A mass of small bubbles
senses.definition: a mass of small white bubbles that forms on the surface of a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 液体表面形成的一大片细小的白色气泡
senses.example: White foam covered the surface of the boiling pot.
senses.exampleCN: 滚开的锅面上覆着一层白色的泡沫。
senses.why: The core image is a crowded layer of bubbles sitting on a liquid, and this is the sense the word names first.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是挤在液体表面的一层气泡，这也是这个词最先命名的义项。

senses.title: To produce foam
senses.definition: to produce a mass of small bubbles, as soap or a shaken drink does
senses.definitionCN: 像肥皂或被摇晃的饮料那样产生大量小气泡
senses.example: The soap foamed quickly in the warm water.
senses.exampleCN: 肥皂在温水里很快起泡。
senses.why: The noun for the bubble layer turns into a verb for the act of making it, with no change of image.
senses.whyCN: 指气泡层的名词直接转成制造这层气泡的动词，意象没有改变。

senses.title: An engineered bubble product
senses.definition: a manufactured liquid or gel full of bubbles, used for shaving, cleaning, or fighting fires
senses.definitionCN: 人工制成的含大量气泡的液体或凝胶，用于剃须、清洁或灭火
senses.example: Crews covered the spilled fuel with foam.
senses.exampleCN: 消防人员用泡沫覆盖了泄漏的燃料。
senses.why: Once industry learns to make stable foams on purpose, the material itself takes the name of its bubbles.
senses.whyCN: 当工业学会有意制造稳定的泡沫后，这种材料本身就直接以「气泡」为名。

senses.title: A solid full of air cells
senses.definition: a spongy solid made of many trapped air cells, such as foam rubber or plastic foam
senses.definitionCN: 由许多封闭气泡组成的海绵状固体，如泡沫橡胶或泡沫塑料
senses.example: The box was lined with soft foam.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子里衬着柔软的海绵。
senses.why: The same bubble structure, frozen into a solid, gives a light material that still looks like a mass of foam.
senses.whyCN: 同样的气泡结构被冻结成固体，就得到一种轻质材料，看起来仍像一团泡沫。

senses.title: The white water of breaking waves
senses.definition: the whitened water of breaking waves, and by literary extension the sea itself
senses.definitionCN: 碎浪形成的白色水花，在文学用法里又引申为大海本身
senses.example: The boat pushed through the foam at the river mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 小船冲过河口处的白浪。
senses.why: Sea water broken into bubbles is the largest natural foam, so poets could use the word for the whole sea.
senses.whyCN: 被浪打碎成气泡的海水是自然界最大的泡沫，诗人便用这个词来指整片大海。

senses.title: To be furious
senses.definition: to show violent anger, as in the phrase foam at the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 表现出极度的愤怒，尤见于「口吐白沫」这一说法
senses.example: He foamed with anger when the plan was rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 计划被否决时，他气得暴跳如雷。
senses.why: In rabies and in extreme rage the mouth actually foams, so the bodily picture becomes a figure for fury.
senses.whyCN: 在狂犬病与极度暴怒时，嘴边确实会泛出白沫，这个身体画面因而成了愤怒的比喻。

intro.en: Foam goes back to Old English fam, a word for froth and for the sea, with Germanic relatives and no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: foam 可追溯到古英语 fām，兼指泡沫与大海，有日耳曼语亲属，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: A deeper Indo-European source for froth is often proposed, but no single reconstructed form is agreed.
items.cn: 常有人为「泡沫」提出更早的印欧语来源，但并无公认的单一重构形式。

items.en: Reconstructed faimaz, meaning foam or froth, is the shared Germanic ancestor.
items.cn: 重构形式 *faimaz 意为泡沫，是日耳曼语各支的共同祖先。

items.en: Fam names foam, froth, and the sea itself.
items.cn: 古英语 fām 指泡沫、浮沫，也指大海。

items.en: The spelling moves through fome toward the modern foam.
items.cn: 拼写经过 fome 逐渐变成现代形式 foam。

items.en: Chemical and steam foams enter industry, cleaning, and firefighting.
items.cn: 化学泡沫与蒸汽泡沫进入工业、清洁与消防。

items.en: Foam rubber and plastic foam give the word a solid, spongy sense.
items.cn: 泡沫橡胶与泡沫塑料使这个词获得「固体海绵材料」的义项。

note.en: Foam belongs to a small family of bubble words, with its own adjectives and close synonyms for froth.
note.cn: foam 属于一小群「气泡」词，既有自己的形容词，也有与「浮沫」相近的同义词。

entries.definitionCN: 布满泡沫的；泡沫状的（foam 加 -y）

entries.definition: producing foam
entries.definitionCN: 正在起泡的；泛着白沫的（foam 加 -ing）

entries.definition: the white foam made by soap and water
foam on the sea, a literary word
entries.definitionCN: 海沫；海浪上的泡沫，属书面语

normalIntro.en: Foam is a layer of trapped air: on beer, on waves, in soap, and finally sealed inside a solid.
normalIntro.cn: foam 是被困住的一层空气：在啤酒上、在浪上、在肥皂里，最后被封进固体里。

normal.en: Foam and froth both name a bubble layer, but foam is often the broader, whiter mass.
normal.cn: foam 与 froth 都指气泡层，但 foam 常指更宽、更白的一大片。

normal.en: Sea foam marks the place where a wave has just broken.
normal.cn: 「sea foam」标出了浪刚刚碎裂的地方。

normal.en: Foam rubber is named for the air cells sealed inside it.
normal.cn: 「foam rubber」得名于封在里面的气泡。

normal.en: Foam at the mouth is literal in illness and figurative in rage.
normal.cn: 「foam at the mouth」在疾病里是实写，在暴怒里是比喻。

normal.en: Shaving foam and firefighting foam are both engineered bubble masses.
normal.cn: 「shaving foam」与「firefighting foam」都是人工设计的泡沫团。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of beer where the white layer stands above the amber liquid.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯啤酒，白色的泡沫层浮在琥珀色液体上面。

abstract.en: Picture a bar of soap leaving a white ring of bubbles in the sink.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肥皂在水池里留下一圈白色气泡。

abstract.en: Picture a nozzle spraying thick white foam over a burning car.
abstract.cn: 想象一支喷嘴把浓白的泡沫喷在燃烧的汽车上。

examples.en: The beer had a thick white foam on top.
examples.cn: 啤酒上面有一层厚厚的白沫。

examples.en: The waves foamed around the rocks.
examples.cn: 浪花在礁石周围泛起白沫。

examples.en: The firefighters covered the burning fuel with foam.
examples.cn: 消防员用泡沫覆盖了燃烧的燃料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「foam」读起来像「浮沫」——浮在液体上面的沫子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fām（泡沫；海）→ 中古英语 fome → 现代英语 foam；与原始日耳曼语重构形式 *faimaz 同源，核心义「液体表面成片的细密气泡」。

sensesIntro.en: Foam begins as bubbles on a liquid, becomes the act of making them, then the manufactured foam, the solid foam, the white water of waves, and finally the foam of extreme rage.
sensesIntro.cn: foam 先指液体表面的气泡，再指产生气泡的动作，随后指人工泡沫、固体泡沫、碎浪的白水，最后指暴怒时的口沫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dense white layer of bubbles resting on a liquid.
core.cn: 核心意象：浮在液体上的一层密密的白色气泡。

branches.en: The bubble layer itself is the root sense.
branches.cn: 气泡层本身是词义的根。

branches.en: Making the layer turns the noun into a verb.
branches.cn: 制造这层气泡，就把名词变成了动词。

branches.en: Human-made foams split into a liquid product and a spongy solid.
branches.cn: 人造泡沫分成液态制剂与海绵状固体两支。

branches.en: The largest natural foam is the white water of the sea.
branches.cn: 自然界最大的泡沫是海上的白浪。

branches.en: Real foam at the mouth becomes the figure for senseless anger.
branches.cn: 嘴边真实的白沫，成了失去理智的愤怒的比喻。

intro.en: Foam is a Germanic noun and verb with a small English family made by the suffixes -y, -ing, and -less.
intro.cn: foam 是日耳曼语来源的名词兼动词，英语中用 -y、-ing、-less 等后缀构成了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Foam has no Latin ancestor; its line runs from Old English fam and reconstructed Germanic faimaz.
latinIntro.cn: foam 没有拉丁语祖先，其脉络从古英语 fām 与日耳曼语重构形式 *faimaz 一脉相承。

definition_zh: 敌人；仇敌；对手；危害之物
definition_en: an enemy, or a person or thing that works against another

sceneCN: 这里 foe 是「敌人」（第 1 个义项：战争或冲突中的敌对一方）；句意：两军在河谷边对峙，侦察兵要辨认前方来的是朋友还是敌人。

pos.zh: 敌人；仇敌；对手；危害之物

derivatives.zh: foe + man 构成的复合名词，义为「敌人」，多见于诗歌与古语
与 foe 同出日耳曼语表示「敌对」的词根，指家族或群体间的世仇，属同源词而非严格派生

senses.title: An enemy in war
senses.definition: a hostile person or army fighting against another in a war
senses.definitionCN: 在战争中与另一方作战的敌方人员或军队
senses.example: The soldiers watched the foe across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们盯着河对岸的敌人。
senses.why: The oldest sense comes straight from the Old English adjective for hostile, so the word first names a wartime enemy.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项直接来自古英语中表示「敌对的」形容词，所以这个词最先指战时的敌人。

senses.title: A personal enemy
senses.definition: a person who hates another and wishes that person harm
senses.definitionCN: 憎恨某人并希望其受到伤害的人
senses.example: He had become a foe of the family that once helped him.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了那个曾经帮助过他的家族的仇人。
senses.why: War hostility shrinks to the scale of two people, and the word now names private hatred as well.
senses.whyCN: 战争层面的敌意缩小到两个人之间，这个词于是也指私人仇恨。

senses.title: An opponent in a contest
senses.definition: a rival or opponent in a game, race, or argument
senses.definitionCN: 比赛、竞速或争论中的对手
senses.example: She beat a stronger foe in the final round.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一轮击败了一位更强的对手。
senses.why: Any structured struggle can borrow the war word, so a rival on a field or in a debate becomes a foe.
senses.whyCN: 任何有规则的较量都可以借用这个战争词，于是赛场或辩论中的对手也被称为 foe。

senses.title: Something harmful to a cause
senses.definition: a person, thing, or condition that works against a stated aim
senses.definitionCN: 阻碍某一明确目标的人、事物或状况
senses.example: Delay is a foe to every rescue plan.
senses.exampleCN: 拖延对每一项救援计划都是大敌。
senses.why: The idea of hostility extends from people to anything that fights against a purpose, such as delay or disease.
senses.whyCN: 敌对的观念从人扩展到任何与目标作对的东西，例如拖延或疾病。

intro.en: Foe comes from Old English fah, meaning hostile or guilty, and from a Germanic root shared with feud; a deeper Indo-European link is debated.
intro.cn: foe 来自古英语 fāh，意为「敌对的；有罪的」，其日耳曼语词根与 feud（世仇）同源；更早的印欧语联系尚有争议。

items.en: A deeper Indo-European root is often proposed, but no single form is accepted.
items.cn: 常有人提出更早的印欧语词根，但没有公认的单一形式。

items.en: Reconstructed faihaz means hostile or malignant.
items.cn: 重构形式 *faihaz 意为「敌对的；怀有恶意的」。

items.en: Fah means hostile, and also guilty or outlawed.
items.cn: 古英语 fāh 既指敌对的，也指有罪的、被剥夺法律保护的。

items.en: Foe settles as the plain noun for an enemy.
items.cn: 中古英语中 foe 固定为表示「敌人」的普通名词。

items.en: The word turns literary and formal, often paired with friend.
items.cn: 这个词变得偏书面、偏正式，常与 friend 对举。

items.en: Modern use keeps foe for wars, rivals, and causes.
items.cn: 现代英语把 foe 保留给战争、对手与事业上的对立面。

note.en: Foe is a formal, mostly literary enemy word, with Germanic relatives and plainer synonyms close by.
note.cn: foe 是偏正式、多用于书面的「敌人」词，旁边既有日耳曼语亲属，也有更朴素的同义词。

entries.definition: an enemy, used mainly in poetry and old writing
entries.definitionCN: 敌人，主要用于诗歌与古旧文字（foe 加 man）

entries.definition: a long bitter quarrel between families or groups
entries.definitionCN: 家族或群体间的长期世仇，与 foe 同源

entries.definition: a thick cloud of water droplets near the ground
entries.definitionCN: 雾；与 foe 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person or country that is hostile to another
entries.definitionCN: 敌对的人或国家，是 foe 最常用的同义词

entries.definition: an opponent in a conflict or contest
a person competing for the same goal
entries.definitionCN: 争夺同一目标的竞争者

normalIntro.en: Foe is the short, hard word for an enemy: it survives mostly in set pairs and in writing that wants a colder tone than enemy.
normalIntro.cn: foe 是「敌人」的短促硬朗说法：它主要活在固定对举与比 enemy 更冷峻的书面文字里。

normal.en: Friend or foe is the sentry question, the pair that keeps foe alive in everyday speech.
normal.cn: 「friend or foe」是哨兵的问句，正是这个对举让 foe 活在日常口语里。

normal.en: Feud and foe share the Germanic root for hostility, so a feud is hostility stretched over years.
normal.cn: feud 与 foe 共享表示敌意的日耳曼语词根，世仇就是把敌意拉长到许多年。

normal.en: Foe belongs to written and poetic English; conversation usually prefers enemy.
normal.cn: foe 属于书面与诗歌英语，日常对话通常更爱用 enemy。

normal.en: Mortal foe and sworn foe both mean an enemy you will never make peace with.
normal.cn: 「mortal foe」与「sworn foe」都指永远不会和解的敌人。

normal.en: Old English fah meant both hostile and guilty, so enmity and blame once shared one word.
normal.cn: 古英语 fāh 兼指敌对的与有罪的，敌意与罪责曾共用一个词。

abstract.en: Picture two banners on opposite banks of a river, each facing the other.
abstract.cn: 想象河两岸各立一面战旗，彼此相对。

abstract.en: Picture two people from one village standing back to back after a quarrel.
abstract.cn: 想象同村的两个人吵翻后背对背站着。

abstract.en: Picture two players across a net, each waiting for the other to fail.
abstract.cn: 想象球网两侧的两名球员，都在等对方失手。

examples.en: The knight rode out to meet his foe.
examples.cn: 骑士策马出城迎敌。

examples.en: Poverty is a foe to good health.
examples.cn: 贫困是健康的敌人。

examples.en: The two teams were old foes on the field.
examples.cn: 这两支队伍在球场上是一对老对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「foe」读起来像「否」——凡是敌对的人，先被一口否掉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fāh（敌对的；有罪的）→ 中古英语 foe（敌人）；与原始日耳曼语重构形式 *faihaz、feud（世仇）同源，核心义「敌对的一方」。

sensesIntro.en: Foe narrows from a wartime enemy to a private enemy, then to a rival in any contest, and finally to anything that fights against a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: foe 从战时的敌人缩到私人仇敌，再扩到任何较量中的对手，最后指任何与某项事业作对的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hostile banners facing each other across a river.
core.cn: 核心意象：河两岸两面敌对的旗子遥遥相对。

branches.en: The wartime enemy is the oldest and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 战时的敌人是最古老、最字面的义项。

branches.en: Hostility between two people gives the private enemy sense.
branches.cn: 两个人之间的敌意给出「私人仇敌」这一义项。

branches.en: A contest borrows the war word for its rival.
branches.cn: 较量借用这个战争词来指对手。

branches.en: Anything that blocks an aim becomes a foe to that aim.
branches.cn: 任何阻碍目标的东西，都成了那个目标的对立面。

branches.en: Both the hated person and the harmful condition carry the same hostile force.
branches.cn: 被憎恨的人与有害的状况，都带着同一种敌对力量。

intro.en: Foe is a Germanic noun with very few English derivatives; its family is mostly compounds and one old synonym.
intro.cn: foe 是日耳曼语来源的名词，英语派生词很少，其词族主要是复合词与一个古老同义词。

latinIntro.en: Foe has no Latin ancestor; the word is Germanic, and Latin expresses the same idea with a different root.
latinIntro.cn: foe 没有拉丁语祖先，属日耳曼语；拉丁语用另一个词根表达「敌人」。

items.example: Old English fah already carried the idea of hostility.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 fāh 已带有敌对的含义。

items.example: The reconstructed faihaz is the Germanic source.
items.exampleCN: 重构形式 *faihaz 是日耳曼语源头。

items.example: Foe is the modern short noun.
items.exampleCN: foe 是现代英语的短名词。

items.example: The plural foes appears in battle reports.
items.exampleCN: 复数 foes 常见于战报。

items.example: Foeman joins foe to man.
items.exampleCN: foeman 由 foe 与 man 合成。

items.example: The suffix -man builds foeman.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -man 构成 foeman。

items.example: Feud and foe come from the same Germanic root.
items.exampleCN: feud 与 foe 出自同一日耳曼语词根。

items.meaning: a person one likes and trusts
items.example: Friend stands opposite foe in the old pair.
items.exampleCN: 在古老的对举里，friend 与 foe 相对。

definition_zh: 有雾的；雾气弥漫的；模糊的；头脑昏沉的
definition_en: full of fog, or unclear and hazy like something seen through fog
core_image: 一扇起雾的窗：玻璃上蒙着白汽，外面的树只剩一团模糊的灰影
scene: 清晨的湖边什么也看不清，对岸的树只剩一团灰影。The foggy morning hid the far shore behind a wall of grey.
sceneCN: 这里 foggy 是「有雾的、雾气弥漫的」（第 1 个义项：空气中充满雾）；句意：有雾的清晨把远岸藏在灰色的雾墙后面。

pos.zh: 有雾的；雾气弥漫的；模糊的；头脑昏沉的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「雾；贴近地面的浓雾」
foggy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「雾气；模糊」
fog 加 -ed 构成，义为「蒙上雾的；被弄糊涂的」

senses.title: Full of fog
senses.definition: having a lot of fog in the air, so that it is hard to see far
senses.definitionCN: 空气中充满雾，以至于看不远
senses.example: It was a foggy morning, and the buses moved slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个有雾的早晨，公交车开得很慢。
senses.why: The suffix -y turns the noun fog into an adjective that simply means full of it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 把名词 fog 变成形容词，字面意思就是「充满雾的」。

senses.title: Vague and hard to recall
senses.definition: not clear or exact, especially of a memory or impression
senses.definitionCN: 不清楚、不确切，尤指记忆或印象
senses.example: I have only a foggy memory of that night.
senses.exampleCN: 我对那一夜只有模糊的记忆。
senses.why: A thing seen through fog loses its edges, so an unclear memory is pictured as foggy.
senses.whyCN: 隔着雾看东西会丢掉轮廓，于是记不清的记忆就被说成 foggy。

senses.title: Unable to think clearly
senses.definition: dazed and unable to think clearly, as after lack of sleep or illness
senses.definitionCN: 昏沉、无法清楚思考，如缺觉或生病之后
senses.example: My mind was still foggy after the long flight.
senses.exampleCN: 长途飞行之后，我的头脑仍然昏沉。
senses.why: The fog moves from the air into the mind, blurring thoughts the way mist blurs a view.
senses.whyCN: 雾从空气里进入头脑，像雾气模糊视野那样模糊思路。

senses.title: Covered with mist or condensation
senses.definition: covered with a thin layer of mist or steam, so that a surface cannot be seen through
senses.definitionCN: 蒙着一层薄雾或水汽，使表面看不清
senses.example: She wiped the foggy mirror with her sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 她用袖子擦掉起雾的镜子。
senses.why: The literal layer of water on glass repeats the weather sense on a small surface.
senses.whyCN: 玻璃上的那层水汽把天气义缩小到一个小表面上重演了一遍。

senses.title: Unclear in outline or expression
senses.definition: lacking a clear shape or meaning, so that it is hard to understand
senses.definitionCN: 形状或意思不清楚，难以理解
senses.example: The plan remained foggy and nobody knew what to do first.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划仍然含混不清，没人知道先做什么。
senses.why: If fog hides a landscape, foggy wording hides the outline of an idea.
senses.whyCN: 雾遮住风景，含混的措辞就遮住一个想法的轮廓。

intro.en: Foggy is fog plus the suffix -y; fog itself is of uncertain origin, perhaps from a Scandinavian word for mist or spray.
intro.cn: foggy 由 fog 加后缀 -y 构成；fog 的词源尚无定论，一般认为可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语中表示薄雾或浪花的词。

items.en: Fog is often traced to Danish fog or a similar Scandinavian word for mist, spray, or snowdrift.
items.cn: fog 常被追溯到丹麦语 fog 或类似的斯堪的纳维亚词，意为薄雾、浪花或雪堆。

items.en: Fog appears in English in the sixteenth century as a word for thick mist close to the ground.
items.cn: 十六世纪，fog 以「贴近地面的浓雾」之义进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -y is added to fog to form foggy, meaning full of fog.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 加到 fog 上构成 foggy，意为充满雾的。

items.en: Writers extend foggy from weather to the mind, speaking of foggy memories and foggy ideas.
items.cn: 十九世纪，作家把 foggy 从天气扩展到头脑，说「模糊的记忆」与「含混的想法」。

items.en: Modern English also uses foggy for misted glass and for unclear plans or outlines.
items.cn: 现代英语里，foggy 也用于起雾的玻璃和含混的计划或轮廓。

note.en: Foggy belongs to the fog family and sits close to misty and hazy; the look-alikes share the same ending.
note.cn: foggy 属于 fog 词族，与「misty」「hazy」意义相邻；形近组共享同样的词尾。

entries.definition: thick mist close to the ground
covered with mist, or confused
the state of being foggy
full of thin mist
unclear because of heat or mist
not clear in shape

normalIntro.en: Foggy is the adjective of fog, and both the weather sense and the mental sense grow from the picture of a misted window.
normalIntro.cn: foggy 是 fog 的形容词，天气义与头脑义都从「起雾的窗」这幅画面长出来。

normal.en: Fog is thick mist, and foggy means full of it.
normal.cn: fog 是浓雾，foggy 就是充满雾的。

normal.en: A foggy morning slows traffic because drivers cannot see far.
normal.cn: 有雾的早晨交通变慢，因为司机看不远。

normal.en: A foggy memory is one whose edges have been lost.
normal.cn: 模糊的记忆就是丢了边缘的记忆。

normal.en: Foggy thinking clears after sleep and fresh air.
normal.cn: 昏沉的思路在睡眠和新鲜空气之后会清醒。

normal.en: Compare misty and hazy: both are thinner and softer than foggy.
normal.cn: 对比 misty 与 hazy：两者都比 foggy 更薄、更柔。

abstract.en: See a window painted white with breath, and the garden behind it reduced to shadows.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇被呼气蒙白的窗，窗后的花园只剩影子。

abstract.en: Watch a photo through smeared glass: the faces lose their edges.
abstract.cn: 透过抹花的玻璃看照片：人脸都丢了轮廓。

abstract.en: Feel wool wrapped around your thoughts, so they move slowly and bump into each other.
abstract.cn: 感觉思想被羊毛裹住，动得慢，还互相碰撞。

examples.en: The valley stays foggy until the sun burns the mist away.
examples.cn: 山谷一直有雾，直到太阳把雾气晒散。

examples.en: He had a foggy idea of what the job involved.
examples.cn: 他对这份工作做什么只有一个模糊的概念。

examples.en: Her glasses went foggy when she came in from the cold.
examples.cn: 她从寒冷的外面进来时，眼镜起了雾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛给」——雾里看不清路，只好请佛给条路；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 fog（雾；词源一般认为来自斯堪的纳维亚语）+ 后缀 -y（充满……的）→ foggy；核心义「被雾裹住、看不清」。

sensesIntro.en: Foggy starts with air full of fog, then moves to unclear memory, a dazed mind, misted surfaces, and vague outlines.
sensesIntro.cn: foggy 从「空气充满雾」开始，再转到模糊的记忆、昏沉的头脑、起雾的表面与含混的轮廓。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window misted white, with the garden behind it reduced to shadows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇蒙白的窗，窗后的花园只剩影子。

branches.en: Weather fog is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 天气的雾是字面义。

branches.en: A memory seen through fog loses its edges.
branches.cn: 隔着雾看记忆，边缘就丢了。

branches.en: The fog moves inside and slows thought.
branches.cn: 雾进入内部，让思路变慢。

branches.en: Misted glass repeats the weather sense on a small surface.
branches.cn: 起雾的玻璃把小范围内的天气义重演一遍。

branches.en: Both thick air and vague wording hide an outline.
branches.cn: 浓雾与含混的措辞都遮住轮廓。

intro.en: Foggy is a native English adjective built from fog with the suffix -y; the family includes fog, fogged, and fogginess.
intro.cn: foggy 是英语本族形容词，由 fog 加后缀 -y 构成；同族词包括「fog」「fogged」与「fogginess」。

latinIntro.en: Fog has no reliable Latin source; the word is generally traced to Scandinavian rather than to Latin.
latinIntro.cn: fog 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，一般认为它来自斯堪的纳维亚语而非拉丁语。

items.example: Fog covered the road.
items.exampleCN: 雾笼罩了道路。

items.example: The morning was foggy.
items.exampleCN: 早晨有雾。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y forms foggy from fog.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 fog 构成 foggy。

items.example: The valley grew foggier at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 黄昏时山谷的雾更浓了。

items.example: This is the foggiest month of the year.
items.exampleCN: 这是一年中雾最浓的月份。

items.example: The lens was fogged by steam.
items.exampleCN: 镜片被蒸汽蒙住了。

items.example: Fogginess made the landing hard.
items.exampleCN: 雾气使降落变得困难。

items.example: He defogged the windscreen before driving.
items.exampleCN: 开车前他给挡风玻璃除了雾。

definition_zh: 阻挠；挫败；箔；金属薄片；陪衬；花剑
definition_en: to stop a plan from succeeding, or a very thin sheet of metal used to set something off
core_image: 伸出的脚被轻轻一绊，原本要走的那一步停在半空
scene: 球赛最后几分钟，后卫伸脚把对方必进的射门挡了出去。A last-minute tackle foiled the striker just as he was about to shoot.
sceneCN: 这里 foil 是「阻挠、挫败」（第 1 个义项：使计划或企图落空）；句意：最后一刻的铲断破坏了前锋的射门。

derivatives.zh: foil 加 -ist 构成，义为「花剑运动员」
foil 加 -ing 构成，义为「阻挠；挫败」
foil 加 -ed 构成，义为「受挫的；贴了箔的」

senses.title: To stop a plan from succeeding
senses.definition: to prevent a plan, attempt, or attack from succeeding
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、企图或攻击无法成功
senses.example: The guard foiled an attempt to enter the building.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫挫败了一次进入大楼的企图。
senses.why: The verb comes from Old French fouler, to trample, so foiling a plan is figuratively treading it down before it can stand.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词来自古法语 fouler（践踏），所以挫败计划就是把它在站稳之前踩下去。

senses.title: A very thin sheet of metal
senses.definition: a very thin sheet of metal, often used to wrap or cover something
senses.definitionCN: 很薄的金属片，常用于包裹或覆盖物品
senses.example: She wrapped the leftovers in aluminium foil.
senses.exampleCN: 她用铝箔把剩菜包起来。
senses.why: This sense has a different source, Latin folium, a leaf, because a foil is as thin as a leaf.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来源不同，出自拉丁语 folium（叶子），因为箔薄得像一片叶子。

senses.title: A contrast that sets something off
senses.definition: a person or thing that makes another seem better by contrast
senses.definitionCN: 通过对比使另一人或物显得更出色的人或物
senses.example: The plain sister served as a foil to the brilliant heroine.
senses.exampleCN: 那位平淡的妹妹衬托出女主角的出色。
senses.why: A thin metal leaf was once placed under a gem to reflect light into it, and that setting-off image became the contrast sense.
senses.whyCN: 过去人们把薄金属片垫在宝石下面把光反上去，这种「衬亮」的画面就变成了对比义。

senses.title: A light fencing sword
senses.definition: a light sword with a blunted point, used in the sport of fencing
senses.definitionCN: 剑尖钝化的轻型剑，用于击剑运动
senses.example: He won the bout with a quick touch of his foil.
senses.exampleCN: 他用花剑快速一点赢得了这一局。
senses.why: The fencing foil is probably named for its blunted, foil-like blade, though the exact link is uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 击剑花剑大概因其钝而薄的剑身得名，但确切的联系仍不确定。

intro.en: English has two foils: the verb to thwart, from Latin fullare, to trample cloth, and the noun for a thin sheet, from Latin folium, a leaf.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个 foil：动词「挫败」来自拉丁语 fullare（踩踏布料），名词「薄片」来自拉丁语 folium（叶子）。

items.en: Fullare means to trample or press cloth, from fullo, a fuller of cloth.
items.cn: fullare 意为踩踏、压平布料，来自 fullo（漂洗工）。

items.en: Fouler carries the trampling sense into Old French.
items.cn: fouler 把「践踏」之义带入古法语。

items.en: Foil enters Middle English as a verb meaning to trample down or defeat.
items.cn: foil 以「踩倒、击败」的动词义进入中古英语。

items.en: Folium, a leaf, gives the thin sheet sense through Old French foille.
items.cn: folium（叶子）经古法语 foille 给出「薄片」义。

items.en: The thin metal sheet appears in the sixteenth century, and the gem setting later adds the contrast sense.
items.cn: 十六世纪出现「金属薄片」，宝石衬底的做法后来又添出「陪衬」义。

items.en: The fencing foil is recorded late in the sixteenth century; its exact origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 击剑花剑在十六世纪后期见于记载，确切来源不确定。

note.en: Foil looks like a family of short English words; the look-alikes share letters, while the near meanings split between thwarting and thin sheets.
note.cn: foil 看起来像一族短小的英语词；形近组共享字母，近义组则分成「挫败」与「薄片」两条线。

entries.definitionCN: 小马（只是拼写相近，词源不同）
