to make a plan fail
thin tin or aluminium sheet

normalIntro.en: Foil has two lives: a trampling verb that means thwart, and a leaf-thin sheet of metal.
normalIntro.cn: foil 有两条命：一条是从「踩踏」来的动词「挫败」，一条是叶子般薄的金属片。

normal.en: To foil a plan is to tread it down before it can stand.
normal.cn: foil a plan 就是在计划站稳之前把它踩下去。

normal.en: Aluminium foil is thin enough to fold around a sandwich.
normal.cn: 铝箔薄得可以裹住一个三明治。

normal.en: A foil in a story sets off the hero by contrast.
normal.cn: 故事里的陪衬人物用对比把主角衬出来。

normal.en: A fencing foil is light and has a blunted point.
normal.cn: 击剑花剑很轻，剑尖是钝的。

normal.en: Remember the split: thwarting comes from fullare, sheeting from folium.
normal.cn: 记住这条分叉：挫败义来自 fullare，薄片义来自 folium。

abstract.en: See a boot come down on a half-built bridge and flatten it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只靴子踩到一座造了一半的桥，把它踩平。

abstract.en: Think of a leaf so thin that light passes through it, then imagine that leaf as metal.
abstract.cn: 想象一片薄得透光的叶子，再把它想成金属。

abstract.en: Picture a grey stone beside a bright gem: the dull one makes the bright one shine.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗亮宝石旁边有一块灰石：暗淡的那块让亮的更亮。

examples.en: The new rules foiled his plan to sell the land.
examples.cn: 新规定挫败了他卖地的计划。

examples.en: Cover the dish with foil before it goes into the oven.
examples.cn: 进烤箱之前用箔纸盖住盘子。

examples.en: The quiet friend was a foil to her loud brother.
examples.cn: 那位安静的朋友衬托出她弟弟的喧闹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛衣欧」——像给佛像披上一件薄薄的金箔衣；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fullare（踩踏、压平）经古法语 fouler → 动词 foil「挫败」；另一支拉丁语 folium（叶子）经古法语 foille → 名词 foil「薄片、箔」，再由宝石衬底引申出「陪衬」。两条来源同形不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Foil begins with the trampling verb that means thwart, then moves to the thin sheet, the contrast it creates under a gem, and the light fencing sword.
sensesIntro.cn: foil 先从「踩踏」来的动词义「挫败」开始，再转到薄金属片、宝石衬底形成的「陪衬」，以及轻型的花剑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boot pressing a half-built bridge flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只靴子把造了一半的桥踩平。

branches.en: Trampling a plan gives the thwarting sense.
branches.cn: 把计划踩下去，得到「挫败」义。

branches.en: The leaf-thin sheet is a separate Latin source.
branches.cn: 叶子般薄的薄片来自另一支拉丁来源。

branches.en: A metal leaf under a gem produces the contrast sense.
branches.cn: 宝石下面的金属薄片产生「陪衬」义。

branches.en: The blunted fencing sword is the sport sense.
branches.cn: 钝刃的击剑用剑是运动义。

branches.en: A foil under a gem is both a thin sheet and a contrast.
branches.cn: 宝石下的箔既是薄片，也是陪衬。

intro.en: Foil draws on two Latin families: fullare, to trample, and folium, a leaf; English builds foiled, foiling, and foilist from them.
intro.cn: foil 汲取两个拉丁词族：fullare（踩踏）与 folium（叶子）；英语由此构成「foiled」「foiling」与「foilist」。

latinIntro.en: Latin fullare means to trample cloth, and Latin folium means a leaf; the two roots meet again in English foil.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fullare 意为踩踏布料，拉丁语 folium 意为叶子；两个词根在英语 foil 里再次相遇。

items.example: Fullare gives the thwarting verb.
items.exampleCN: fullare 给出「挫败」这个动词。

items.example: Fullo names the worker who treads cloth.
items.exampleCN: fullo 指踩踏布料的工匠。

items.example: Fouler carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: fouler 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Foil means to tread a plan down.
items.exampleCN: foil 意为把计划踩下去。

items.example: Folium gives the thin sheet sense.
items.exampleCN: folium 给出「薄片」义。

items.example: Foille passes the sheet sense to English.
items.exampleCN: foille 把「薄片」义传给英语。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms foiled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 foiled。

items.meaning: a fencer who uses a foil
items.example: Foilist names the fencer.
items.exampleCN: foilist 指花剑运动员。

definition_zh: 煽动；挑起；助长；热敷
definition_en: to stir up trouble or strong feeling, or in older medicine to apply warmth to the body
core_image: 一块温热的湿布敷在皮肤上，热气一寸寸往里渗，把里面的东西催得动起来
scene: 村口有人散播谣言，几句话就把人群的不满点着了。Rumours about the missing grain helped foment unrest in the village.
sceneCN: 这里 foment 是「煽动、激起」（第 1 个义项：鼓动骚乱或不满）；句意：关于粮食失踪的谣言在村里煽起了不安。

derivatives.zh: foment 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「煽动；热敷疗法」
foment 加 -er 构成，义为「煽动者」

senses.title: To stir up unrest
senses.definition: to stir up trouble, unrest, or strong feeling in other people
senses.definitionCN: 在他人中挑起麻烦、动乱或强烈情绪
senses.example: The pamphlets helped foment revolt in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这些小册子帮助在首都煽起了反抗。
senses.why: Latin fomentum was a warm poultice; heat applied to the skin was imagined as heat applied to a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fomentum 是温热的敷剂；敷在皮肤上的热，被想象成加在人群上的热。

senses.title: To stir up a feeling or suspicion
senses.definition: to encourage a feeling such as suspicion, fear, or resentment to grow
senses.definitionCN: 促使猜疑、恐惧或怨恨等情绪滋长
senses.example: A few careless words fomented suspicion among the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 几句不慎的话在邻居之间助长了猜疑。
senses.why: A poultice keeps warmth in one place so that something develops there, and a rumour works the same way on a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 敷剂把热留在一处，让那里的东西长起来；谣言对一种情绪起的作用正是如此。

senses.title: To apply warmth as a treatment
senses.definition: to apply warm water, cloth, or medicine to a part of the body, as in older medical practice
senses.definitionCN: 把温水、热布或药物敷在身体某处，如旧时的医疗做法
senses.example: The nurse fomented the swollen knee with warm cloths.
senses.exampleCN: 护士用热布敷在肿胀的膝盖上。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: fomentum was literally a warm application, and the modern word keeps it as a medical term.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：fomentum 本义就是温热的敷剂，现代英语把它保留为医学术语。

senses.title: To keep a situation going
senses.definition: to encourage a situation or process to continue and grow stronger
senses.definitionCN: 促使某种局面或过程继续并加强
senses.example: Delay only fomented the anger that the first mistake had started.
senses.exampleCN: 拖延只是助长了最初那个错误引发的怒火。
senses.why: The warmth of the poultice does not create heat from nothing; it keeps and spreads heat that is already there, and so does fomenting.
senses.whyCN: 敷剂的热不是凭空生出的，而是把已有的热留住、散开；foment 也是如此。

intro.en: Foment comes from Latin fomentum, a warm poultice, from fovere, to warm or cherish; it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: foment 来自拉丁语 fomentum（温热的敷剂），源于 fovere（使暖、珍爱）；经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Fovere means to warm, keep warm, or cherish.
items.cn: fovere 意为使暖、保温、珍爱。

items.en: Fomentum is a warm application or poultice.
items.cn: fomentum 是温热的敷剂。

items.en: Fomentare means to apply warmth or to stir something up.
items.cn: fomentare 意为施以温热，或把某事发起来。

items.en: Fomenter carries the word into French with both the medical and the stirring sense.
items.cn: fomenter 把这个词连同医学义与「激起」义带入法语。

items.en: Foment appears in English in the fifteenth century, first as a medical term.
items.cn: 十五世纪，foment 以医学术语的身份出现在英语中。

items.en: Modern English drops the poultice from daily use and keeps the figurative sense of stirring up trouble.
items.cn: 现代英语在日常生活中舍弃了敷剂义，保留了「挑起事端」的比喻义。

note.en: Foment belongs to the fovere family and sits close to incite and stir up; the look-alikes share the -ment ending.
note.cn: foment 属于 fovere 词族，与「incite」「stir up」意义相邻；形近组共享 -ment 词尾。

entries.definition: to undergo fermentation, or to be in restless excitement
entries.definitionCN: 发酵；（情绪）沸腾（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a very short period of time
entries.definitionCN: 片刻；瞬间（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a spoken or written remark
entries.definitionCN: 评论；意见（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to urge someone to act, especially violently
to start trouble or a course of action
to cause a reaction, often anger

normalIntro.en: Foment is a warm poultice that became a metaphor: heat applied to a feeling makes it grow.
normalIntro.cn: foment 是一贴温热的敷剂，后来成了比喻：加在情绪上的热会让它长起来。

normal.en: Foment unrest and you heat a crowd until it moves.
normal.cn: foment unrest 就是把人群加热到动起来。

normal.en: Foment suspicion and a small doubt grows into distrust.
normal.cn: foment suspicion 就是让一点怀疑长成不信任。

normal.en: The old doctor fomented a sore knee with warm cloths.
normal.cn: 老医生用热布敷肿痛的膝盖。

normal.en: Compare incite: incite urges people to act, foment heats the feeling behind the act.
normal.cn: 对比 incite：incite 催促人行动，foment 加热行动背后的情绪。

normal.en: The -ation ending marks the noun fomentation, the act of fomenting.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ation 标记名词 fomentation，即「煽动、热敷」的行为。

abstract.en: See a hot cloth laid on a crowded square, and the whole square begins to steam and move.
abstract.cn: 想象一块热布铺在拥挤的广场上，整个广场开始冒热气、动起来。

abstract.en: Picture a small coal kept warm under ash until it glows red.
abstract.cn: 想象一块小火炭被灰焐着，直到烧红。

abstract.en: Feel a warm poultice on a stiff knee, and the tightness slowly loosens.
abstract.cn: 感觉一块温热的敷布贴在僵硬的膝盖上，绷紧的地方慢慢松开。

examples.en: The speech was designed to foment anger against the new tax.
examples.cn: 这篇演讲意在煽起对新税的不满。

examples.en: Small delays fomented doubt about the whole project.
examples.cn: 一再的小延误助长了对整个项目的怀疑。

examples.en: In older medicine, doctors fomented the chest with hot herbs.
examples.cn: 在旧时的医学里，医生用热草药敷胸口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛门特」——像庙里一贴热敷布，把情绪焐得发烫；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fovere（使暖、珍爱）→ fomentum（温热敷剂）→ fomentare（施热；激起）→ 古法语 fomenter → 英语 foment；核心义「用热把东西催起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Foment starts with the warm poultice of Latin fomentum, then moves from stirring a crowd to stirring a feeling, applying heat as medicine, and keeping a situation alive.
sensesIntro.cn: foment 从拉丁语 fomentum 的温热敷剂出发，再从煽动人群转到挑起情绪、以热施治，以及让一种局面持续下去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm cloth laid on the skin, with heat spreading inward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块温热的布敷在皮肤上，热气往里渗。

branches.en: Heat on a crowd is the political sense.
branches.cn: 加在人群上的热，是政治义。

branches.en: Heat kept in one feeling makes it grow.
branches.cn: 热留在一处情绪里，就让它长起来。

branches.en: The literal poultice is the old medical sense.
branches.cn: 字面的敷剂是古老的医学义。

branches.en: Warmth that spreads keeps a situation going.
branches.cn: 散开的热让一种局面持续下去。

branches.en: Both unrest and suspicion are feelings heated until they act.
branches.cn: 动乱与猜疑都是被加热到发作的情绪。

intro.en: Foment comes from the Latin fovere family, with fomentation and fomenter built on the same stem.
intro.cn: foment 来自拉丁语 fovere 词族，「fomentation」与「fomenter」都建在同一个词干上。

latinIntro.en: Latin fovere means to warm or cherish, and fomentum is the warm cloth itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fovere 意为使暖、珍爱，fomentum 就是那块温热的布。

items.example: Fovere gives the warmth at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: fovere 提供这个词核心的「暖」。

items.example: Fomentum is the cloth that carries the heat.
items.exampleCN: fomentum 就是带着热的那块布。

items.meaning: to apply warmth, to stir up
items.example: Fomentare adds the sense of stirring.
items.exampleCN: fomentare 添上「激起」的意思。

items.example: Fomenter brings the word into French.
items.exampleCN: fomenter 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: to stir up, to apply warmth
items.example: Foment keeps both the medical and the political sense.
items.exampleCN: foment 同时保留医学义与政治义。

items.example: Fomentation names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: fomentation 指这种行为本身。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms fomentation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 fomentation。

items.example: Fomenting keeps the verb alive in compounds.
items.exampleCN: fomenting 让这个动词在组合中保持活力。

definition_zh: 喜爱；钟爱；偏爱；柔情
definition_en: a warm affection or liking for a person or thing
core_image: 掌心轻轻覆在旧照片上，指尖停在那个人的脸旁
scene: 母亲站在床边，看着熟睡的孩子。She watched her son sleep with a fondness that she could not hide.
sceneCN: 这里 fondness 是「喜爱、钟爱」（第 1 个义项：对某人的温柔感情）；句意：她看着熟睡的儿子，藏不住满心的喜爱。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「深情的；痴爱的」
fond 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「深情地；温柔地」
over 加 fond，义为「过分溺爱的」

senses.title: Warm affection for a person
senses.definition: a gentle, warm affection that someone feels for another person
senses.definitionCN: 对另一个人怀有的温柔而深厚的感情
senses.example: She has always had a fondness for her younger brother.
senses.exampleCN: 她一直很疼爱自己的弟弟。
senses.why: Fond once meant foolishly doting, so fondness began as the doting side of love and later softened into warm affection.
senses.whyCN: fond 原意是「痴心地爱」，所以 fondness 最初指痴爱的一面，后来才软化为温柔的喜爱。

senses.title: A strong liking for a thing
senses.definition: a strong liking for a particular thing, food, place, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某样东西、某种食物、某个地方或某项活动的强烈喜好
senses.example: He has a fondness for strong tea and long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 他偏爱浓茶和长距离散步。
senses.why: The feeling does not need a person as its object, so the word easily names a taste for things and habits.
senses.whyCN: 这种感情不必以人为对象，于是这个词自然也能指对事物与习惯的喜好。

senses.title: Tenderness shown in manner
senses.definition: a tender warmth that shows in the way someone speaks or looks
senses.definitionCN: 在言语或神情中流露出来的那股温柔
senses.example: There was a fondness in her voice when she mentioned the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 她提到那座老房子时，声音里有一种温情。
senses.why: Because fondness is a feeling, it can also name the visible warmth that the feeling lends to a voice or a glance.
senses.whyCN: 因为 fondness 是一种感情，它也能指这种感情赋予声音或目光的可见温柔。

senses.title: Doting indulgence
senses.definition: an attachment so warm that it excuses faults or weakens judgment
senses.definitionCN: 热到会为缺点开脱、削弱判断力的依恋
senses.example: His fondness for his eldest son made him overlook every mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他对长子的溺爱让他对每一个过错都视而不见。
senses.why: The old sense of foolish doting survives here: affection so strong that it makes the lover blind.
senses.whyCN: 古义「痴心的溺爱」在此留存：感情强到让喜爱的人看不见缺点。

senses.title: Foolish credulity in old use
senses.definition: an archaic sense: foolish trust or a doting, credulous nature
senses.definitionCN: 古旧义项：愚笨的轻信，或痴迷而轻信的天性
senses.example: In older writing, fondness could mean the credulity of a fool.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的文本里，fondness 可以指愚人的轻信。
senses.why: The adjective fond first meant foolish, so the noun once named foolishness itself before affection took over.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 fond 最初意为「愚笨的」，所以这个名词先指愚笨本身，后来才被「喜爱」占据。

intro.en: Fondness is fond plus the noun suffix -ness; the adjective goes back to Middle English fonned, which meant foolish.
intro.cn: fondness 由形容词 fond 加名词后缀 -ness 构成；fond 可上溯到中古英语 fonned（愚笨的）。

items.en: Fonned, the past participle of fonnen, means foolish or silly.
items.cn: fonned 是动词 fonnen 的过去分词，意为愚笨的、傻的。

items.en: Fond shifts from foolish to doting, and then to simply affectionate.
items.cn: fond 从「愚笨」转为「痴心的」，再转为单纯的「深情」。

items.en: The suffix -ness turns the adjective into the noun fondness.
items.cn: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成名词 fondness。

items.en: Fondness settles into warm affection and everyday liking.
items.cn: fondness 稳定为温柔的喜爱与日常的喜好。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as fondness for carry the word into letters, memoirs, and everyday speech.
items.cn: fondness for 一类固定搭配把这个词带进书信、回忆录与日常口语。

note.en: Fondness belongs to the fond family and sits close to affection, liking, and attachment.
note.cn: fondness 属于 fond 词族，与 affection、liking、attachment 意义相邻。

entries.definition: affectionate and doting
with affection
too indulgent
a gentle feeling of liking or love
a feeling of enjoyment or taste for something
a strong feeling of being fond of someone

normalIntro.en: Fondness is built from fond and -ness, and the whole family keeps the idea of a heart that has grown warm.
normalIntro.cn: fondness 由 fond 加 -ness 构成，整个词族始终带着「心变暖了」的意思。

normal.en: Fondness adds -ness to fond, just as darkness adds -ness to dark.
normal.cn: fondness 是 fond 加 -ness，正如 darkness 是 dark 加 -ness。

normal.en: A fond look is a warm look, and fondness is that warmth itself.
normal.cn: 「fond look」是温柔的目光，而 fondness 就是那份温柔本身。

normal.en: To have a fondness for something is to like it in a settled, gentle way.
normal.cn: 「have a fondness for」某物，就是以安稳而温柔的方式喜欢它。

normal.en: Fondly is the adverb, so to remember fondly is to remember with fondness.
normal.cn: fondly 是副词，所以「remember fondly」就是带着 fondness 去回忆。

normal.en: Compare liking: liking is plainer, while fondness is warmer and often a little old-fashioned.
normal.cn: 对比 liking：liking 更平实，fondness 更温暖，也常带一点旧时的味道。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that rests on a photograph and does not want to move away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在照片上，久久不愿移开。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of strong tea that someone asks for every single morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯浓茶，有人每个清晨都要点它。

abstract.en: Picture a voice that softens when an old house is mentioned.
abstract.cn: 想象提到一座老房子时，声音不自觉地软了下来。

examples.en: Her fondness for old films grew stronger every winter.
examples.cn: 她对老电影的喜爱每年冬天都更深一些。

examples.en: He still speaks of his first teacher with fondness.
examples.cn: 他谈起第一位老师时仍满怀温情。

examples.en: The fondness between the two sisters survived every quarrel.
examples.cn: 两姐妹之间的感情经受住了每一次争吵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fondness」听来像「放的你思」——心里总也放不下一个人，这份放不下就是喜爱；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: fond（中古英语 fonned，愚笨的、痴心的）＋ -ness（名词后缀）→ fondness；核心义从「痴心」软化为「温柔的喜爱」。

sensesIntro.en: Fondness starts as affection for a person, extends to a liking for things, shows itself as tenderness, and keeps an older shade of doting and foolish trust.
sensesIntro.cn: fondness 先指对人的喜爱，再扩及对事物的偏好，外显为温情，并保留了「溺爱」与「愚笨轻信」的旧日色彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand resting on an old photograph, unwilling to move away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在旧照片上，久久不愿移开。

branches.en: Affection for a person is the centre of the word.
branches.cn: 对人的喜爱是这个词的核心。

branches.en: Liking for food, places, and habits extends the feeling to things.
branches.cn: 对食物、地方与习惯的喜好把这种感情扩展到事物上。

branches.en: Tenderness is the feeling made visible in a voice or a look.
branches.cn: 温情是这种感情在声音或目光中的外露。

branches.en: Doting indulgence and old foolish credulity both come from the foolish edge of fond.
branches.cn: 溺爱与旧义的愚笨轻信，都来自 fond 的「愚」这一面。

branches.en: Both a person and a thing can be the object of fondness.
branches.cn: 人与事物都可以是 fondness 的对象。

intro.en: Fondness is a native English noun built from the adjective fond, with a small and old family around it.
intro.cn: fondness 是英语本土名词，由形容词 fond 加后缀构成，周围是一个小而古老的词族。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin source here: fond goes back to Middle English fonned, of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族没有可靠的拉丁语来源：fond 可上溯到中古英语 fonned，更早的来源不确定。

items.example: Fond describes a warm heart.
items.exampleCN: fond 描述一颗温暖的心。

items.example: Fonnen is the old verb behind fond.
items.exampleCN: fonnen 是 fond 背后那个古老的动词。

items.example: Fonned first gave fond its foolish sense.
items.exampleCN: fonned 最早赋予 fond「愚笨」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness turns fond into fondness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 把 fond 变成 fondness。

items.example: Fondness names the feeling itself.
items.exampleCN: fondness 指这种感情本身。

items.example: Fondly is how a fond person acts.
items.exampleCN: fondly 是深情之人的行事方式。

items.example: Overfond adds the idea of too much.
items.exampleCN: overfond 添上了「过多」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms fondly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 fondly。

items.example: Fondness for is the most common pattern.
items.exampleCN: fondness for 是最常见的搭配模式。

definition_zh: 食品；食物原料；粮食
definition_en: a substance that people eat or use as food, especially one handled as a material or as goods
core_image: 仓库里一袋袋米面和罐头堆到天花板，等着装车
scene: 洪水退去后，救援仓库里堆满了成袋的米面。Workers counted the foodstuffs before loading the trucks.
sceneCN: 这里 foodstuff 是「粮食、食品货物」（第 3 个义项：成批储存和运输的食品）；句意：工人们装车前清点了这些粮食。

derivatives.zh: 复合词的前一半，泛指一切食物
food 加 -ie，口语指热衷美食的人
feed 与 stuff 组合，专指动物饲料

senses.title: Food as a substance
senses.definition: a substance that people eat or that is used as food
senses.definitionCN: 供人食用或用作食物的物质
senses.example: Rice is the chief foodstuff in many parts of Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 稻米是亚洲许多地方的主要食物。
senses.why: Food names what is eaten and stuff names material, so the compound first means the material of eating.
senses.whyCN: food 指吃的东西，stuff 指材料，所以这个复合词首先指「吃的材料」。

senses.title: Raw material for cooking or processing
senses.definition: a basic material that is prepared or processed into food
senses.definitionCN: 经过烹制或加工而成为食物的基础材料
senses.example: The factory turns raw foodstuffs into ready meals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把食材原料变成即食餐。
senses.why: Because stuff points to raw material, the word also names what cooking and industry start from.
senses.whyCN: 因为 stuff 强调原材料，这个词也指烹饪与工业加工的起点。

senses.title: Food handled as goods
senses.definition: food of this kind gathered in bulk, stored, shipped, or traded
senses.definitionCN: 成批收集、储存、运输或买卖的这类食品
senses.example: Aid agencies shipped foodstuffs to the flooded villages.
senses.exampleCN: 救援机构把粮食运往被洪水围困的村庄。
senses.why: Once such material is gathered in bulk and moved as cargo, the compound takes on a commercial and countable sense.
senses.whyCN: 当这类材料成批收集并作为货物运输时，这个复合词就有了商业与可数的用法。

senses.title: A food item on a list
senses.definition: a single item or category of food named in nutrition, trade rules, or customs lists
senses.definitionCN: 在营养、贸易规则或海关清单中被逐项列出的食品
senses.example: Every foodstuff on the label must be declared to customs.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上的每一种食品都必须向海关申报。
senses.why: Regulation and nutrition treat each substance as a unit to be listed, so the word comes to name an item rather than a meal.
senses.whyCN: 法规与营养学把每种物质当作一个单位来列明，于是这个词指清单上的一项，而不是一顿饭。

intro.en: Foodstuff joins the Old English word for food to stuff, a word for material that came into English through French.
intro.cn: foodstuff 把古英语的「食物」一词与经法语传入的 stuff（材料）组合在一起。

items.en: Fod means food, and the verb fodian means to feed.
items.cn: fod 意为食物，动词 fodian 意为喂养。

items.en: Estoffe means material or provisions, and English borrows it as stuff.
items.cn: estoffe 意为材料或给养，英语借作 stuff。

items.en: Food and stuff begin to be used together for the material of eating.
items.cn: food 与 stuff 开始连用，指可供食用的材料。

items.en: Foodstuff settles as a compound noun for substances used as food.
items.cn: foodstuff 固定为复合名词，指用作食物的物质。

items.en: The plural foodstuffs spreads through trade, aid, and nutrition writing.
items.cn: 复数 foodstuffs 在贸易、救援与营养文本中广泛使用。

note.en: Foodstuff is a compound of food and stuff, and it sits near provisions, groceries, and nourishment.
note.cn: foodstuff 是 food 与 stuff 的复合词，与 provisions、groceries、nourishment 义域相邻。

entries.definition: what people eat
material or things in general
animal feed
supplies of food kept for a journey or a group
entries.definitionCN: 为行程或一群人储备的食物

entries.definition: food and household goods bought from a shop
entries.definitionCN: 从商店买来的食品与日用杂货

entries.definition: food that keeps a body healthy
entries.definitionCN: 维持身体健康的滋养食物

normalIntro.en: Foodstuff is simply food plus stuff: the stuff that is food, seen as material rather than as a meal.
normalIntro.cn: foodstuff 就是 food 加 stuff：当作材料的食物，而不是端上桌的菜。

normal.en: Foodstuff is food plus stuff, and stuff here means material.
normal.cn: foodstuff 是 food 加 stuff，这里的 stuff 指材料。

normal.en: A foodstuff is bought, stored, and shipped, while a dish is cooked and served.
normal.cn: foodstuff 被采购、储存、运输，而 dish 是被烹制、端上桌的。

normal.en: Staple foodstuffs are the everyday base of a diet.
normal.cn: 「staple foodstuffs」是日常饮食的基础。

normal.en: Perishable foodstuffs spoil quickly and need cold storage.
normal.cn: 「perishable foodstuffs」容易变质，需要冷藏。

normal.en: Compare provisions: foodstuff is neutral and technical, while provisions suggest supplies kept for a journey.
normal.cn: 对比 provisions：foodstuff 中性而技术化，provisions 偏指为行程储备的给养。

abstract.en: Picture a sack of rice opened in a kitchen, showing the grain itself rather than the cooked meal.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房里打开的一袋米，看到的是米本身，而不是做好的饭。

abstract.en: Picture a cook sorting raw materials on a board before the fire is lit.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师在点火之前，把原料摊在案板上分类。

abstract.en: Picture a crate marked with a weight, waiting on a dock for a ship.
abstract.cn: 想象一只标着重量的板条箱，停在码头上等船。

examples.en: The region exports foodstuffs such as rice, tea, and dried fish.
examples.cn: 该地区出口大米、茶叶和鱼干等食品。

examples.en: Nutritionists list every foodstuff that may cause an allergy.
examples.cn: 营养学家列出每一种可能引起过敏的食品。

examples.en: Prices of basic foodstuffs rose sharply last year.
examples.cn: 去年基本食品的价格大幅上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「foodstuff」听来像「福得食」——有福气就得到食物，这份福气里的吃食就是食品；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: food（古英语 fod，食物）＋ stuff（古法语 estoffe，材料、给养）→ foodstuff，核心义「可当作食物的材料」。

sensesIntro.en: Foodstuff begins as the material of eating, narrows to raw ingredients, then to bulk goods, and finally to an item on a list.
sensesIntro.cn: foodstuff 从「可吃的材料」出发，收窄为食材原料，再指成批货物，最后指清单上的一项食品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sacks of grain stacked to the ceiling in a warehouse.
core.cn: 核心意象：仓库里一袋袋粮食堆到天花板。

branches.en: The plain substance that people eat is the first sense.
branches.cn: 供人食用的物质是第一个义项。

branches.en: Raw material that cooking and industry start from is the second sense.
branches.cn: 烹饪与工业加工的原材料是第二个义项。

branches.en: Material gathered in bulk and shipped as cargo is the commercial sense.
branches.cn: 成批收集并作为货物运输的材料是商业义项。

branches.en: A single listed substance is the countable, regulatory sense.
branches.cn: 清单上单独列出的一项物质是可数、法规化的义项。

branches.en: Both the plain substance and the shipped cargo are foodstuffs in the counting sense.
branches.cn: 单纯的食物与运输的货物，在可数用法里都是 foodstuff。

intro.en: Foodstuff is a transparent compound of food and stuff, and both parts still carry their own meaning.
intro.cn: foodstuff 是 food 与 stuff 的透明复合词，两部分仍各自保留含义。

latinIntro.en: Neither part comes from Latin: food is Old English, and stuff arrived through Old French from an uncertain source.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不来自拉丁语：food 是古英语词，stuff 经古法语传入，更早的来源不确定。

items.example: Food is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: food 是这个复合词的前一半。

items.example: Fod is the older form of food.
items.exampleCN: fod 是 food 较早的形式。

items.example: Fodian means to give food.
items.exampleCN: fodian 意为供给食物。

items.example: Stuff supplies the material half of the word.
items.exampleCN: stuff 提供这个词「材料」的那一半。

items.example: Estoffe is the French source of stuff.
items.exampleCN: estoffe 是 stuff 的法语来源。

items.example: The suffix -s forms foodstuffs.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成 foodstuffs。

items.example: Foodstuff joins the two halves.
items.exampleCN: foodstuff 把两半结合起来。

items.example: Foodstuffs is the usual form in trade.
items.exampleCN: foodstuffs 是贸易中的常用形式。

items.example: Feedstuff swaps food for feed.
items.exampleCN: feedstuff 把 food 换成 feed。

definition_zh: 强行的；使用暴力的；有说服力的；强烈的
definition_en: done or carried out by force, or strong enough to compel attention or belief
core_image: 一只手从外面把门硬推开，门闩应声断裂
scene: 法庭上，律师指出房东没有通知就换锁进门。The judge ruled that the entry by the landlord was forcible and unlawful.
sceneCN: 这里 forcible 是「强行的」（第 1 个义项：违背他人意愿、靠力量做成）；句意：法官裁定房东这次进入属于强行进入，不合法。

pos.zh: 强行的；使用暴力的；有说服力的；强烈的

derivatives.zh: forcible 加 -ly，义为「强行地；用力地」
基础名词，义为「力量；武力」
forcible 加 -ness，义为「强制性；有力」

senses.title: Done by force
senses.definition: done or achieved by physical power or threats, against resistance
senses.definitionCN: 靠体力或威胁、在有人反抗的情况下做成的
senses.example: The court condemned the forcible removal of the tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 法院谴责对租户的强行驱离。
senses.why: Forcible joins force to the suffix -ible, so it describes whatever is done by force rather than by consent.
senses.whyCN: forcible 由 force 加后缀 -ible 构成，因此指靠力量而非征得同意做成的事。

senses.title: Carried out with violence
senses.definition: carried out with violent physical action that may injure people
senses.definitionCN: 以可能伤人的暴力动作实施的
senses.example: The guards used forcible measures to clear the crowded hall.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫动用暴力手段清空了拥挤的大厅。
senses.why: When the force used turns physical and hurts people, the same adjective names violent action.
senses.whyCN: 当所用的力量变成会伤人的身体动作时，同一个形容词就指暴力行为。

senses.title: Strong enough to convince
senses.definition: clear and strong enough to convince the mind or to overcome doubt
senses.definitionCN: 清晰有力，足以说服人心或排除疑虑的
senses.example: She made a forcible argument for raising the minimum wage.
senses.exampleCN: 她为提高最低工资提出了有力的论证。
senses.why: Latin fortis means strong, and a strong reason overpowers doubt, so forcible also means convincing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fortis 意为「强」，强硬的道理能压过疑虑，所以 forcible 也指有说服力。

senses.title: Strong in effect or style
senses.definition: strikingly strong in its effect, sound, or manner
senses.definitionCN: 在效果、声音或方式上显得格外强烈的
senses.example: The empty classroom was a forcible reminder of the missing students.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的教室强烈地提醒人们那些缺席的学生。
senses.why: The old sense of fortis as sheer strength survives in descriptions of powerful effect, sound, or style.
senses.whyCN: fortis 原有「纯粹的力量」之义，这层意思留存在对强烈效果、声音或风格的描述里。

intro.en: Forcible comes from Latin fortis, strong, through force and the suffix -ible, which marks what can be done.
intro.cn: forcible 来自拉丁语 fortis（强），经 force 与后缀 -ible 构成，词尾表示「能被……的」。

items.en: Fortis means strong, and fortia means strength.
items.cn: fortis 意为强，fortia 意为力量。

items.en: The verb fortire means to strengthen, and the noun force spreads through popular Latin.
items.cn: 动词 fortire 意为使强壮，名词 force 在通俗拉丁语中传开。

items.en: Force means strength or violence, and forcible forms beside it.
items.cn: force 意为力量或暴力，forcible 在它旁边形成。

items.en: Forcible enters English and describes what is done against resistance.
items.cn: forcible 进入英语，描述违背反抗做成的事。

items.en: The sense of a convincing argument grows out of the idea of strong reason.
items.cn: 「有说服力的论证」这一义项从「强有力的道理」发展而来。

items.en: Legal phrases such as forcible entry keep the physical sense in daily use.
items.cn: forcible entry 一类法律短语让「体力强制」的义项留在日常使用中。

note.en: Forcible shares its root with force and forcibly, and it is easily confused with forceful.
note.cn: forcible 与 force、forcibly 同根，也容易与 forceful 混淆。

entries.definition: strength or power used on someone
by force
full of strength and energy
required by rule or law
using physical force to hurt people
able to persuade

normalIntro.en: Forcible is force plus -ible: the stem says the action is done by force, and the ending says it can be done to someone.
normalIntro.cn: forcible 是 force 加 -ible：词干表示靠力量行事，词尾表示「能施加于某人」。

normal.en: Forcible is force plus -ible, the same pattern as visible and sensible.
normal.cn: forcible 是 force 加 -ible，与 visible、sensible 属同一构词模式。

normal.en: forcible entry, forcible removal, and forcible means all keep the physical sense.
normal.cn: 「forcible entry」「forcible removal」「forcible means」都保留体力强制的意思。

normal.en: Forcibly is the adverb: to act forcibly is to act by force.
normal.cn: forcibly 是副词，「act forcibly」就是靠力量行事。

normal.en: Keep forcible and forceful apart: forcible means done by force, while forceful means full of energy.
normal.cn: 区分 forcible 与 forceful：forcible 指靠力量做成，forceful 指充满气势。

normal.en: A forcible argument is one that pushes doubt aside by sheer strength.
normal.cn: 「forcible argument」指靠力量把疑虑推到一边的论证。

abstract.en: Picture a door pushed open from outside until the bolt breaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被从外面推到门闩断裂。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd being pushed back by a line of shields.
abstract.cn: 想象一排盾牌把人群向后推。

abstract.en: Picture a single sentence that makes a noisy room go quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话让喧闹的房间安静下来。

examples.en: The law forbids forcible entry into a private home.
examples.cn: 法律禁止强行进入私人住宅。

examples.en: He was removed from the meeting by forcible means.
examples.cn: 他是被强制手段带离会场的。

examples.en: Her speech was a forcible call for reform.
examples.cn: 她的演讲是一次有力的改革呼吁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「force」是力量，「-ible」是「能……的」——能靠力量办成的，就是强行的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fortis（强、有力）→ 晚期拉丁语 fortia（力量）→ 古法语 force（力量；暴力）＋ -ible（能……的）→ forcible，核心义「凭力量做成的」。

sensesIntro.en: Forcible moves from action done by force, to violent action, to a reason strong enough to convince, and finally to any strong effect.
sensesIntro.cn: forcible 从「靠力量做成」出发，转到暴力行为，再指足以服人的道理，最后泛指强烈的效果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a door until the bolt gives way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把门推到门闩断裂。

branches.en: Action done against resistance is the first and legal sense.
branches.cn: 违背反抗做成的事，是第一个也是法律上的义项。

branches.en: Physical violence is that action at its roughest.
branches.cn: 身体暴力是这种动作最粗野的形态。

branches.en: A strong reason compels the mind, so compulsion turns into conviction.
branches.cn: 强有力的道理能压住心思，于是「强制」转成「说服」。

branches.en: Strong effect in sound or style keeps the idea of sheer strength.
branches.cn: 声音或风格上的强烈效果，保留的正是「纯粹的力量」这个想法。

branches.en: Both the legal phrase and the violent act describe force applied from outside.
branches.cn: 法律短语与暴力行为都描述从外部施加的力量。

intro.en: Forcible is built on the Latin stem fortis, strong, through force and the suffix -ible.
intro.cn: forcible 建在拉丁词干 fortis（强）之上，经由 force 与后缀 -ible 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis means strong, and fortia means strength; both feed the French and English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 意为强，fortia 意为力量，二者共同哺育了法语与英语的词族。

items.example: Fortis is the strength at the bottom of the family.
items.exampleCN: fortis 是这个词族底层的「强」。

items.example: Fortia gives the noun force its meaning.
items.exampleCN: fortia 赋予名词 force 力量的含义。

items.example: Fortire means to make strong.
items.exampleCN: fortire 意为使变强。

items.example: Force is the stem of forcible.
items.exampleCN: force 是 forcible 的词干。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms forcible.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ible 构成 forcible。

items.example: Forcible keeps the passive pattern of -ible.
items.exampleCN: forcible 保留了 -ible 的被动意味。

items.example: Forcibly adds the adverb ending.
items.exampleCN: forcibly 加上了副词词尾。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms forcibly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 forcibly。

items.example: Forceful uses -ful instead of -ible.
items.exampleCN: forceful 用的是 -ful 而不是 -ible。

definition_zh: 最重要的；首要的；最前面的；最先的
definition_en: most important, or placed ahead of all others in place, time, or rank
core_image: 一队人走在路上，最前面那一个走在所有人之前，所有目光都落在他身上
scene: 修房子的钱还没着落，大家开会时把这件事写在了白板最上面。The foremost question is how to pay for the repairs.
sceneCN: 这里 foremost 是「最重要的、排在最前的」（第 1 个义项：最重要的）；句意：最要紧的问题是修房子的钱从哪里来。

pos.zh: 最重要的；首要的；最前面的

derivatives.zh: 「fore + front」复合而成，指最前的位置或最前线
foremost 的基础词，指前面的；也可作副词表示在前面
fore 的比较级形式，指前一个的、从前的

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: more important than any other thing in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某一情形中比任何其他事情都重要
senses.example: Safety is our foremost concern.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是我们最关心的事。
senses.why: The suffix -most is a superlative ending, so the word places its subject at the very top of a scale of importance.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -most 是最高级词尾，所以这个词把所指对象推到重要性尺度的最顶端。

senses.title: Furthest forward in place
senses.definition: placed ahead of all others in physical space
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上位于所有其他事物之前
senses.example: The foremost carriage of the train was almost empty.
senses.exampleCN: 火车最前面的一节车厢几乎是空的。
senses.why: The fore- element means front, and -most marks the extreme, so foremost first meant the physical front of a line.
senses.whyCN: fore- 表示「前面」，-most 表示极端，所以 foremost 最初指队列里实际的最前端。

senses.title: Earliest in time
senses.definition: coming before all others in time or sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或顺序上先于所有其他事物到来
senses.example: The foremost settlers cleared the land along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 最早到来的定居者开垦了河边的土地。
senses.why: A row in space is easy to read as a row in time, so the earliest member of a series takes the front place.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的一排很容易被读成时间上的一串，于是序列中最早的一员就占住最前的位置。

senses.title: Highest in rank
senses.titleCN: 地位最高的；级别最高的
senses.definition: holding the highest position in a group or hierarchy
senses.definitionCN: 在一个群体或等级体系中占据最高位置
senses.example: She is the foremost diplomat of her generation.
senses.exampleCN: 她是同代人里地位最高的外交官。
senses.why: Rank is pictured as a vertical queue, and whoever stands at the head of that queue is foremost.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成一条竖着的队列，谁站在这条队列的最前端，谁就是 foremost。

senses.title: Standing out among a group
senses.titleCN: 在群体中居首的；首屈一指的
senses.definition: recognised as leading when compared with others of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类相比被认为居于领先地位
senses.example: He is foremost among the critics of the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 在新计划的批评者当中，他位居首位。
senses.why: The pattern foremost among compares one member with a group and sets that member at the front of the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 「foremost among」这一结构把某个人放进群体里比较，并把这个人放在比较的最前面。

senses.title: Before all else, as an adverb
senses.definition: used as an adverb to mean before anything else is done
senses.definitionCN: 作副词使用，表示在做任何别的事之前
senses.example: Foremost, we must thank the volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，我们必须感谢志愿者。
senses.why: English lets a bare modifier stand at the head of a sentence, and that loose position turned the adjective into an adverb of priority.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许不带标记的修饰语站在句首，这个松散的位置使形容词变成了表示优先的副词。

senses.title: At the head of a procession
senses.definition: walking or placed at the front of a line of people or vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 走在或位于人群、车辆队伍的最前方
senses.example: The foremost marchers carried a long red banner.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍最前面的人举着一面长长的红旗。
senses.why: A procession is the clearest picture of a front position, so this sense keeps the oldest spatial meaning alive.
senses.whyCN: 游行队伍最能画出「最前位置」的画面，所以这一义项让最古老的空间含义继续活着。

senses.title: In the fixed phrase first and foremost
senses.definition: in the phrase first and foremost, meaning more than anything else
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法「first and foremost」中，表示胜过其他一切
senses.example: First and foremost, the new law protects children.
senses.exampleCN: 首要的一点是，新法律保护儿童。
senses.why: Placing first beside foremost doubles the idea of priority, and the pair hardened into a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 把 first 与 foremost 并排放，等于把「优先」说了两遍，这一对词于是凝固成固定说法。

intro.en: Foremost is an Old English compound of fore, in front, with the superlative ending -most.
intro.cn: foremost 是古英语复合词，由表示「在前面」的 fore 与最高级词尾 -most 组成。

items.en: The reconstructed root per- supplies the sense of before or in front for the fore- element.
items.cn: 重构词根 per- 为 fore- 这一成分提供「在前」的含义。

items.en: Fore means before or in front, and -mest is the superlative ending of the period.
items.cn: 古英语 fore 意为在前面，-mest 是当时表示最高级的词尾。

items.en: Formest, the early shape of foremost, names the first in place or rank.
items.cn: foremost 的早期形式 formest 指位置上或等级上最前的那个。

items.en: The spelling settles toward foremost, and the word keeps both the spatial and the ranking senses.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 foremost，这个词同时保留空间与等级两层含义。

items.en: Foremost extends to abstract importance, and first and foremost becomes a fixed phrase of priority.
items.cn: foremost 扩展到抽象的重要性，first and foremost 成为表示优先的固定说法。

note.en: Foremost belongs to the fore- family for front positions, and it stands near words for leading or principal.
note.cn: foremost 属于表示「前面」的 fore- 词族，同时与表示「领先、首要」的词相邻。

entries.definition: situated in front, or to the front
the first of two things, or belonging to the past
the leading or most advanced position
most successful or important in a field
entries.definitionCN: 在某领域中最成功或最重要的

entries.definition: first in importance among several things
entries.definitionCN: 在若干事物中最重要的

entries.definition: more important than anything else
entries.definitionCN: 高于一切的；至为重要的

normalIntro.en: Foremost is a queue word: fore- puts it in front and -most pushes it to the extreme end.
normalIntro.cn: foremost 是个「队列词」：fore- 把它放在前面，-most 又把它推到最末端。

normal.en: Fore- means front, so the foremost thing sits at the front of the queue.
normal.cn: fore- 表示前面，所以 foremost 的东西就坐在队列的最前面。

normal.en: -Most is the superlative ending seen in topmost and utmost.
normal.cn: -most 是最高级词尾，topmost 与 utmost 里都能见到它。

normal.en: First and foremost is the fixed phrase for the top priority.
normal.cn: 「first and foremost」是表示最优先事项的固定说法。

normal.en: Foremost among means leading inside a group.
normal.cn: 「foremost among」表示在一个群体里居首。

normal.en: Compare former: former is the comparative of fore, foremost the superlative.
normal.cn: 对比 former：former 是 fore 的比较级，foremost 是最高级。

abstract.en: Picture a long queue and one figure standing at its very head.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的队伍，有一个人站在最前端。

abstract.en: Imagine a ship pushing its nose through thick fog.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船用船头推开浓雾。

abstract.en: Think of the first stone laid in a long line of stones.
abstract.cn: 想象一长排石头里最先放下的那一块。

examples.en: She is the foremost expert on coral reefs in the region.
examples.cn: 她是该地区珊瑚礁方面最权威的专家。

examples.en: First and foremost, the team must agree on a budget.
examples.cn: 首要的一点是，团队必须先就预算达成一致。

examples.en: The foremost coach of the train was kept for the guards.
examples.cn: 火车最前面的车厢留给押车人员使用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛嘛斯特」——想象一尊佛站在队伍最前面，因此它最重要；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fore（前面）+ -most（最高级后缀）→ foremost，字面是「最靠前的」，由空间的最前端引申为地位与重要性最高。

sensesIntro.en: Foremost starts at the front of a physical line, moves to the earliest point in time, climbs to the top of a rank, and ends as a word for top importance.
sensesIntro.cn: foremost 从实际队列的最前端出发，转到时间上的最早，再爬到等级的最高处，最后成为表示最高重要性的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure standing at the very head of a queue.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在队伍的最前端。

branches.en: Top importance is the abstract end of the scale.
branches.cn: 最高重要性是这条尺度的抽象一端。

branches.en: The front of an object and the front of a procession share one picture.
branches.cn: 物体的前端与队伍的前列共享同一个画面。

branches.en: A line in time is read from the same front position.
branches.cn: 时间上的序列也按同一个「最前」位置来读。

branches.en: Rank and comparison both put the leading member at the head.
branches.cn: 等级与比较都把领先的一员放在最前面。

branches.en: The adverb and the fixed phrase carry the priority sense into speech.
branches.cn: 副词用法与固定说法把「优先」的含义带进口语。

intro.en: Foremost is built from the fore- element for front and the superlative ending -most, and the same pieces appear in forefront, forehead, and foreword.
intro.cn: foremost 由表示「前面」的 fore- 与最高级词尾 -most 构成，同样的部件也出现在 forefront、forehead 与 foreword 里。

latinIntro.en: Old English fore is generally taken to be cognate with Latin pro, both going back to an ancient word for before or in front.
latinIntro.cn: 一般认为古英语 fore 与拉丁语 prō 同源，二者都可追到表示「在前」的古老词根。

items.example: Fore- appears in forefront and foreword.
items.exampleCN: fore- 出现在 forefront 与 foreword 里。

items.example: -Most forms topmost and utmost.
items.exampleCN: -most 构成 topmost 与 utmost。

items.example: Fore is the base of foremost.
items.exampleCN: fore 是 foremost 的基础词。

items.example: Foremost joins fore with -most.
items.exampleCN: foremost 把 fore 与 -most 结合在一起。

items.example: Forefront keeps the front image.
items.exampleCN: forefront 保留了「前面」的意象。

items.meaning: the front part of the head
items.example: Forehead is the front of the head.
items.exampleCN: forehead 是头的前部。

items.meaning: a short introduction placed before a book
items.example: Foreword is the word placed before the book.
items.exampleCN: foreword 是放在书前面的话。

items.example: Forebear keeps the sense of earlier times.
items.exampleCN: forebear 保留了「更早」的含义。

items.meaning: the first of two, or of the past
items.example: Former is the comparative of fore.
items.exampleCN: former 是 fore 的比较级。

items.example: Forecast uses fore- in the sense of beforehand.
items.exampleCN: forecast 里的 fore- 表示「预先」。

definition_zh: 先驱；先行者；前身；前兆
definition_en: a person or thing that comes before another and prepares the way for it
core_image: 一个人先跑在大队人马前面，替后来的人探路
scene: 在摩托车流行之前，街上先跑着一种带小发动机的自行车。The bicycle was the forerunner of the motorbike.
sceneCN: 这里 forerunner 是「前身、先驱事物」（第 3 个义项：前身；先驱事物）；句意：自行车是摩托车的前身。

collocations.phrase: a forerunner of things to come
the forerunner of the modern computer

derivatives.zh: 「fore + run」构成的动词，指先于某事发生、预示
forerun 加 -ing 构成的形容词，指先行的、先到的

senses.title: A runner who goes ahead
senses.definition: a person who runs ahead of a group, especially in order to lead the way
senses.definitionCN: 跑在队伍前面的人，尤指为了带路
senses.example: The forerunner reached the ridge long before the others.
senses.exampleCN: 先跑的那个人比其他人早很久到达山脊。
senses.why: Forerunner is a plain compound of fore, in front, and runner, one who runs, so the first sense is wholly literal.
senses.whyCN: forerunner 就是 fore（在前面）与 runner（跑的人）的直白复合，所以第一个义项完全是字面义。

senses.title: A herald sent ahead
senses.definition: a person sent ahead to announce that someone important is coming
senses.definitionCN: 被派到前面，宣告某位重要人物即将到来的人
senses.example: A forerunner rode into the village to announce the king.
senses.exampleCN: 一名先行者骑马进村通报国王即将到来。
senses.why: On a royal journey the rider who went ahead carried the news, and the compound came to name that task.
senses.whyCN: 在王室出巡时，先骑马到前面的人负责传达消息，这个复合词于是也命名了这项任务。

senses.title: An early predecessor of a thing
senses.definition: something that came before a later thing and helped to make it possible
senses.definitionCN: 先于后来事物出现、并促成其诞生的事物
senses.example: The bicycle was the forerunner of the motorbike.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车是摩托车的前身。
senses.why: Once the word named a person who goes before, it easily named any thing that goes before another in history.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指走在前面的人，就很容易指历史上先于另一物出现的东西。

senses.title: The first model of a product
senses.definition: the earliest version of a machine or product that later models improve on
senses.definitionCN: 机器或产品最早的版本，后来的型号在此基础上改进
senses.example: That clumsy machine was the forerunner of every laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 那台笨重的机器是所有笔记本电脑的雏形。
senses.why: An early model literally runs before the finished product, so the same word covers it.
senses.whyCN: 早期型号确实跑在成品之前，所以同一个词也能涵盖它。

senses.title: A sign of something coming
senses.definition: a sign or warning that something is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 表明某事即将发生的迹象或警示
senses.example: Small tremors are often the forerunners of a big quake.
senses.exampleCN: 小震动常常是大地震的前兆。
senses.why: What runs ahead of an event can be a warning rather than a person, and this sense grew from that picture.
senses.whyCN: 跑在一件事前面的，可以是警示而不一定是人，这一义项就从那个画面长出来。

senses.title: A writer who prepares a movement
senses.definition: an artist or thinker whose early work makes a later movement possible
senses.definitionCN: 早期作品为后来流派铺路的艺术家或思想家
senses.example: She is a forerunner of the modern dance style.
senses.exampleCN: 她是现代舞蹈风格的先驱。
senses.why: A person who goes first in time does the same work as a person who goes first in space.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上走在最前的人，和在空间上走在最前的人做的是同一件事。

senses.title: An ancestor in a family line
senses.definition: a person from whom a family or group is descended
senses.definitionCN: 某个家族或群体的先辈
senses.example: Their forerunners crossed the sea three centuries ago.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的祖先在三个世纪前渡海而来。
senses.why: A family line is another queue in time, and the people at its far end are the forerunners.
senses.whyCN: 家族谱系是另一条时间上的队列，站在最远端的人就是 forerunner。

senses.title: A religious figure who prepares the way
senses.definition: a person who prepares people for a religious leader or event
senses.definitionCN: 为某位宗教领袖或某个事件预先预备人心的人
senses.example: John the Baptist is called the forerunner of Christ.
senses.exampleCN: 施洗约翰被称为基督的先行者。
senses.why: Religious language uses the word for anyone who clears the road for a greater figure.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言用这个词指任何为更伟大的人物开辟道路的人。

intro.en: Forerunner is a transparent English compound of fore, in front, and runner, one who runs.
intro.cn: forerunner 是一个透明的英语复合词，由表示「在前面」的 fore 与表示「跑的人」的 runner 组成。

items.en: The reconstructed root per- supplies the sense of before or in front behind fore.
items.cn: 重构词根 per- 为 fore 提供「在前」的含义。

items.en: Fore means before or in front of, and it already forms compounds with nouns of place.
items.cn: 古英语 fore 意为在……之前，并已能与表地点的名词构成复合词。

items.en: Forerunner is recorded in the sense of a person who runs ahead or announces another.
items.cn: forerunner 有记载的最早含义是先跑在前或替他人通报的人。

items.en: Religious writing applies the word to John the Baptist as the one who prepares the way.
items.cn: 宗教写作把这个词用在施洗约翰身上，指那位预备道路的人。

items.en: The word widens to any early predecessor, from machines to ideas, and to signs of what is coming.
items.cn: 这个词扩大到任何早期前身，从机器到思想，也指即将到来之事的征兆。

note.en: Forerunner joins the fore- family with words about running, and it stands close to words for predecessors and early signs.
note.cn: forerunner 以 fore- 与表示「跑」的词结合，并与表示「前身、先兆」的词相邻。

entries.definition: in front, or before
a person or thing that runs
to go before and prepare the way
something that comes before and signals a later thing
entries.definitionCN: 先于某物出现并预示它的东西

entries.definition: the person or thing that held a place before another
a sign of what will happen in the future

normalIntro.en: Forerunner is a picture word: fore- puts the runner at the front of the line.
normalIntro.cn: forerunner 是个画面词：fore- 把跑的人放在队伍的最前面。

normal.en: Fore- means in front, and runner means someone who runs.
normal.cn: fore- 表示在前面，runner 表示跑的人。

normal.en: The plural forerunners often names the early signs of an event.
normal.cn: 复数 forerunners 常指某件事的早期迹象。

normal.en: The pattern a forerunner of is the usual way to name a predecessor.
normal.cn: 「a forerunner of」是命名前身事物的常见结构。

normal.en: Compare forerun: the verb simply means to go before.
normal.cn: 对比 forerun：这个动词就表示走在前面。

normal.en: Religious English uses forerunner for the man who prepares the way.
normal.cn: 宗教英语用 forerunner 指那位预备道路的人。

abstract.en: Picture a scout running half a mile ahead of the column.
abstract.cn: 想象一名侦察兵跑在大部队前面半英里的地方。

abstract.en: Imagine a trumpeter riding into a village before the king arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一名号手在国王到达之前骑马进村。

abstract.en: Think of an old wooden wheel that came before the rubber tyre.
abstract.cn: 想象在橡胶轮胎之前出现的那种旧木轮。

examples.en: The abacus was a forerunner of the calculator.
examples.cn: 算盘是计算器的前身。

examples.en: Dark clouds are often forerunners of a storm.
examples.cn: 乌云常常是暴风雨的前兆。

examples.en: The small protest was a forerunner of a much larger movement.
examples.cn: 那场小小的抗议是规模大得多的运动的前兆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛软呢」——想象一个人跑在队伍最前面，鞋底都跑软了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fore（在前面）+ runner（跑的人）→ forerunner，字面是「先跑在前的人」，由先探路的人引申为前身、先驱与先兆。

sensesIntro.en: Forerunner begins as a person who runs or rides ahead, then becomes any earlier thing that prepares a later one, and finally any sign of what is coming.
sensesIntro.cn: forerunner 最初指先跑或先骑马到前面的人，随后指任何为后来事物铺路的先行者，最后指即将到来之事的征兆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scout running ahead of the column to show the way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一名侦察兵跑在大部队前面为大家指路。

branches.en: The literal runner is the picture at the front of the chain.
branches.cn: 字面上先跑的人，是这条链最前端的画面。

branches.en: The herald adds news to the act of going first.
branches.cn: 通报者给「走在前面」这一动作加上了消息。

branches.en: A predecessor and a first model are the same thing seen in history and in products.
branches.cn: 前身与雏形是同一件事在历史里与在产品里的两种看法。

branches.en: A warning sign is what runs ahead of an event rather than of a person.
branches.cn: 前兆是跑在事件之前而不是跑在人之前的东西。

branches.en: Artists, ancestors, and religious figures all go first for others.
branches.cn: 艺术家、祖先与宗教人物都是替别人先走一步的人。

intro.en: Forerunner is built from fore-, the agent ending -er, and the verb run, and the same pieces appear in forerun, forerunning, and runner.
intro.cn: forerunner 由 fore-、表施事的词尾 -er 与动词 run 构成，同样的部件也出现在 forerun、forerunning 与 runner 里。

latinIntro.en: Old English fore is generally taken to be cognate with Latin pro and prae, while the runner element has no Latin relative.
latinIntro.cn: 一般认为古英语 fore 与拉丁语 prō、prae 同源；而表示「跑」的那一部分在拉丁语里没有同族词。

items.example: Fore- marks whatever comes first.
items.exampleCN: fore- 标记最先出现的东西。

items.example: Run is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: run 是这个复合词的基础。

items.example: Runner adds -er to run.
items.exampleCN: runner 在 run 后加了 -er。

items.meaningCN: 表示施动者的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -er turns verbs into doers.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把动词变成做这件事的人。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms forerunning.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 forerunning。

items.meaning: to go before and prepare the way
items.example: Forerun is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: forerun 是这个名词背后的动词。

items.example: Forerunning events came first.
items.exampleCN: 先行的事件先发生。

items.example: Forerunner joins fore- with runner.
items.exampleCN: forerunner 把 fore- 与 runner 结合起来。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 先跑的人；先驱（与英语 runner 并非同源）

definition_zh: 预见；预知；预料
definition_en: to know or say that something will happen before it actually does
core_image: 人站在今天，眼睛已经看到了明天将要发生的事
scene: 老船长看了看天边的云，就知道午后会有风暴。Sailors used to foresee a storm from the shape of the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里 foresee 是「预知、预见」（第 1 个义项：预知将要发生的事）；句意：水手过去能凭云的形状预见风暴。

derivatives.zh: 「foresee + -able」构成，指能够被提前看到的、可预见的
「un- + foreseen」构成，指没有被提前看到的、意外的
「fore + sight」复合而成，指看见未来的能力、先见之明

senses.title: To know that something will happen
senses.definition: to know or believe that an event will happen before it takes place
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生之前就知道或相信它会发生
senses.example: Some animals seem to foresee a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 有些动物似乎能预知风暴。
senses.why: The fore- element adds before to see, so the word is literally to see beforehand.
senses.whyCN: fore- 给 see 加上了「之前」，所以这个词字面上就是「事先看到」。

senses.title: To predict from evidence
senses.definition: to say what will happen by reasoning from present signs or data
senses.definitionCN: 根据现有迹象或数据推断将会发生什么
senses.example: Analysts foresee a slow recovery next year.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士预测明年会缓慢复苏。
senses.why: Seeing ahead can rest on evidence rather than on magic, and this sense covers reasoned prediction.
senses.whyCN: 往前看可以靠证据而不是靠法术，这一义项涵盖有推理的预测。

senses.title: To anticipate a problem
senses.definition: to think of a difficulty in advance so that it can be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 提前想到某个困难，以便能够应对
senses.example: The planners failed to foresee the shortage of water.
senses.exampleCN: 规划者没有预先想到水源短缺。
senses.why: Looking ahead is most useful when it spots trouble, so the verb often takes a problem as its object.
senses.whyCN: 往前看最有用的时候是发现麻烦，所以这个动词常以问题作宾语。

senses.title: To see the consequences
senses.definition: to understand what an action or decision will lead to
senses.definitionCN: 理解某个行动或决定会导致什么结果
senses.example: Few voters foresaw the cost of the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有选民看出新政策的代价。
senses.why: The word can look past the event itself to the chain of results that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以越过事件本身，看到紧随其后的那一串结果。

senses.title: To plan ahead
senses.definition: to arrange things now on the basis of what is expected later
senses.definitionCN: 依据对以后的预期，现在就做出安排
senses.example: A good captain foresees where the ship will need fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 好船长会预先想到船在哪里需要补给燃料。
senses.why: Knowing the future is only useful if it changes what you do now, and this sense names that use.
senses.whyCN: 知道未来只有改变了当下的行动才有用，这一义项命名的正是这种用途。

senses.title: To sense danger coming
senses.definition: to feel that harm is near before there is clear proof
senses.definitionCN: 在找到明确证据之前就感到伤害临近
senses.example: She foresaw the danger and left the building.
senses.exampleCN: 她预感到危险，离开了那栋楼。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is plain seeing, and a feeling of danger is the body seeing ahead.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是「看见」，而对危险的感受是身体在往前看。

senses.title: Unforeseen: not expected
senses.definition: used of events that were not known or expected before they happened
senses.definitionCN: 用于指在发生之前未被知道或预料到的事件
senses.example: An unforeseen delay kept the train in the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 一次未预见到的延误让火车停在隧道里。
senses.why: The negative participle unforeseen adds un- to the past participle and names what nobody saw coming.
senses.whyCN: 否定分词 unforeseen 在过去分词前加 un-，指没有人看到会来的事。

senses.title: Foreseeable: able to be predicted
senses.definition: able to be known in advance, used of events that can reasonably be expected
senses.definitionCN: 能够提前知道的，用于指可以合理预料的事件
senses.example: The breakdown was entirely foreseeable.
senses.exampleCN: 这次故障完全是可以预见到的。
senses.why: The suffix -able turns the verb into an adjective and marks what can be seen ahead.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把动词变成形容词，标记出能够被提前看到的事。

intro.en: Foresee is an Old English compound of fore, before, and seon, to see, and it has meant to see beforehand for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: foresee 是古英语复合词，由表示「在之前」的 fore 与表示「看见」的 seon 组成，一千多年来一直表示「事先看到」。

items.en: The reconstructed root per- is the source of the fore- element and its sense of before.
items.cn: 重构词根 per- 是 fore- 及其「在前」含义的来源。

items.en: Foreseon joins fore with seon, to see, and means to see beforehand.
items.cn: foreseon 把 fore 与表示「看见」的 seon 结合，意为事先看到。

items.en: Forseen keeps the literal sense of seeing an event before it arrives.
items.cn: 中古英语 forseen 保留「事件到来之前就看到它」的字面意义。

items.en: The modern spelling foresee appears, and the meaning extends from sight to reasoned prediction.
items.cn: 现代拼写 foresee 出现，词义从「看到」扩展到有推理的预测。

items.en: Unforeseen and foreseeable become common adjectives in law, planning, and everyday speech.
items.cn: unforeseen 与 foreseeable 成为法律、规划与日常语言里的常用形容词。

note.en: Foresee belongs to the fore- family with words about knowing the future, and it stands near words for predicting.
note.cn: foresee 属于 fore- 词族中表示「知道未来」的一支，并与表示「预测」的词相邻。

entries.definition: the ability to see what is likely to happen
entries.definitionCN: 看出可能发生之事的能力；先见之明

entries.definition: to be an early sign of a later event
entries.definitionCN: 成为后来事件的早期迹象；预示

entries.definition: to say what will happen in the future
entries.definitionCN: 说出将来会发生的事；预言

entries.definition: to say that an event will happen
to expect something and act before it happens
entries.definitionCN: 预料某事并在它发生前行动

entries.definition: to picture a future situation as likely
entries.definitionCN: 把未来的情形设想为可能发生

normalIntro.en: Foresee is see with before attached: the eye reaches the event before the event arrives.
normalIntro.cn: foresee 就是给 see 加上「之前」：眼睛在事件到来之前就够到了它。

normal.en: Fore- means before, and see means to see.
normal.cn: fore- 表示在之前，see 表示看见。

normal.en: Foresee is literally to see before the event happens.
normal.cn: foresee 字面上就是在事件发生之前看到它。

normal.en: The past tense foresaw follows the same pattern as saw.
normal.cn: 过去式 foresaw 与 saw 的变化方式一致。

normal.en: Unforeseen means nobody saw it coming.
normal.cn: unforeseen 表示没有人看到它会来。

normal.en: Compare foresight: the noun names the ability, the verb names the act.
normal.cn: 对比 foresight：名词指这种能力，动词指这种动作。

abstract.en: Picture an eye at the top of a tall mast looking over the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼睛长在高高桅杆的顶端，越过地平线往前看。

abstract.en: Imagine a weather map with an arrow pointing to tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，箭头指向明天。

abstract.en: Think of a traveller packing an umbrella before leaving.
abstract.cn: 想象一名旅人在出发前就把伞放进了包里。

examples.en: No one could foresee how fast the river would rise.
examples.cn: 没有人能预见河水会上涨得多快。

examples.en: The engineers foresaw the weakness in the design.
examples.cn: 工程师们预见到了设计中的弱点。

examples.en: The report had not foreseen such a sharp fall in sales.
examples.cn: 那份报告没有预料到销量会跌得这么厉害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛系」——像佛一样静静坐着，却早已知晓明天会发生什么；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fore（在之前）+ seon（看见）→ foresee，字面是「事先看见」，由亲眼看到引申为凭迹象推断、预先打算。

sensesIntro.en: Foresee begins as seeing an event before it arrives, widens to prediction from evidence, and covers the planning and the derived forms that follow from knowing the future.
sensesIntro.cn: foresee 从事件到来之前就看见它出发，扩展到凭证据预测，并涵盖由此产生的预先安排与派生形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye that reaches tomorrow before tomorrow arrives.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只在明天到来之前就够到明天的眼睛。

branches.en: Plain knowing is the closest sense to the literal picture.
branches.cn: 单纯的「知道」是最贴近字面画面的义项。

branches.en: Prediction adds reasoning to the act of seeing ahead.
branches.cn: 预测给「往前看」这一动作加上了推理。

branches.en: Problems and consequences are what the eye is usually looking for.
branches.cn: 困难与后果正是这只眼睛通常在找的东西。

branches.en: Planning and a sense of danger turn knowing into action.
branches.cn: 预先安排与危险预感把「知道」变成行动。

branches.en: The negative and the adjective forms name what was or was not seen ahead.
branches.cn: 否定形式与形容词形式命名被看到或没被看到的将来之事。

intro.en: Foresee is built from the fore- element for beforehand plus see, and the same pieces appear in foresight, foreshadow, and foretell.
intro.cn: foresee 由表示「预先」的 fore- 与 see 构成，同样的部件也出现在 foresight、foreshadow 与 foretell 里。

latinIntro.en: Old English fore is generally taken to be cognate with Latin pro and prae, while the element see has no Latin relative.
latinIntro.cn: 一般认为古英语 fore 与拉丁语 prō、prae 同源；而表示「看见」的那一部分在拉丁语里没有同族词。

items.example: Fore- marks what happens earlier.
items.exampleCN: fore- 标记更早发生的事。

items.meaning: to perceive with the eyes or the mind
items.example: See is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: see 是这个复合词的基础。

items.example: Foresee joins fore- with see.
items.exampleCN: foresee 把 fore- 与 see 结合起来。

items.meaning: the ability to see what is coming
items.example: Foresight joins fore- with sight.
items.exampleCN: foresight 把 fore- 与 sight 结合起来。

items.example: The suffix -able forms foreseeable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 foreseeable。

items.example: Foreseeable describes what can be seen ahead.
items.exampleCN: foreseeable 描述能够被提前看到的事。

items.example: Unforeseen adds un- to foreseen.
items.exampleCN: unforeseen 在 foreseen 前加了 un-。

items.example: Foretell uses the same fore- sense.
items.exampleCN: foretell 用的是同一个 fore- 含义。

items.meaning: to be an early sign of
items.example: Foreshadow points to a later event.
items.exampleCN: foreshadow 指向后来发生的事件。

items.meaning: a short introduction before a book
items.example: Foreword shows the front sense of fore-.
items.exampleCN: foreword 显示 fore- 表示「前面」的那层含义。

definition_zh: 可预见的；可预料的；能预料到的
definition_en: able to be known, expected, or anticipated before it happens
core_image: 站在高处，提前看见山脚将要发生的事
scene: 工程开工前，团队已经把能想到的问题全列了出来。Before the project began, the team listed every foreseeable problem.
sceneCN: 这里「foreseeable」是「可预见的」（第 1 个义项：能提前预料到的）；句意：开工前，团队已经把能想到的问题全列了出来。

derivatives.zh: 由 fore-（在前）与 see（看见）构成，义为「预见」
由 foresee 加 -er 构成，义为「预见者」
由 un- 加 foreseeable 构成，义为「不可预见的」
由 foreseeable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可预见性」
由 foreseeable 加 -ly 构成，义为「可预见地」

senses.title: Able to be anticipated
senses.definition: possible to know or expect before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前就能知道或预料到的
senses.example: The outcome was foreseeable from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 结果从一开始就是可以预见的。
senses.why: Fore- adds the idea of beforehand to see, so foreseeable describes what the mind can see ahead of time.
senses.whyCN: fore- 给 see 加上「事先」的意思，所以 foreseeable 描述的是头脑能提前看见的事。

senses.title: Expected within the near future
senses.definition: expected to happen within the period that people can plan for
senses.definitionCN: 预计会在人们能够规划的这段时间内发生
senses.example: Prices will rise in the foreseeable future.
senses.exampleCN: 在可预见的未来，价格会上涨。
senses.why: The phrase the foreseeable future limits planning to the span a person can reasonably look ahead.
senses.whyCN: 「the foreseeable future」把规划限制在一个人能合理前瞻的时间范围内。

senses.title: Anticipated by a reasonable person
senses.definition: within the range of harm or risk that a reasonable person could anticipate
senses.definitionCN: 在一个理性的人能够预料的损害或风险范围之内
senses.example: The court asked whether the damage was foreseeable.
senses.exampleCN: 法院询问这项损害是否属于可预见的范围。
senses.why: Law turns the general idea into a test of responsibility: a person answers for what could be anticipated.
senses.whyCN: 法律把一般性的「可预见」变成责任标准：人要为能够预料到的后果负责。

intro.en: Foreseeable joins fore-, the Old English word for before, with see and the Latin suffix -able, so it literally means able to be seen ahead.
intro.cn: foreseeable 由 fore-（古英语「在前」）、see（看见）和拉丁语后缀 -able（能……的）组成，字面义为「能事先看见的」。

items.en: Fore means before, in front of, or beforehand.
items.cn: fore 意为「在……之前」「在……前面」或「事先」。

items.en: Seon means to see with the eyes or with the mind.
items.cn: seon 意为用眼睛看见，也指用头脑看见。

items.en: Foreseon combines the two into the verb to see beforehand.
items.cn: foreseon 把两者合成动词，意为「事先看见」。

items.en: The suffix -abilis, taken through Old French as -able, means capable of.
items.cn: 后缀 -abilis 经古法语 -able 进入英语，意为「能……的」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century, foreseeable names what can be anticipated.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，foreseeable 用来指能够被预料到的事情。

note.en: Foreseeable belongs to the family of foresee and foresight, and it stands close to predictable and expected.
note.cn: foreseeable 属于 foresee、foresight 这一词族，意义上靠近 predictable 与 expected。

entries.definition: to see or know something before it happens
the ability to anticipate what may happen
not able to be anticipated
entries.definitionCN: 不可预见的；无法预料的

entries.definition: able to be guessed or expected in advance
thought likely to happen
probable or expected

normalIntro.en: Foreseeable is built from fore, see, and able; the word pictures a mind that can look ahead.
normalIntro.cn: foreseeable 由 fore、see、able 三部分构成，画面是一颗能向前看的头脑。

normal.en: Fore means before, so foresee is to see before.
normal.cn: fore 表示「在前」，所以 foresee 就是提前看见。

normal.en: Add -able and you get able to be seen before, hence foreseeable.
normal.cn: 加上 -able，就成了「能被提前看见的」，也就是可预见的。

normal.en: In the foreseeable future covers the stretch of time a planner can look ahead.
normal.cn: 「in the foreseeable future」指规划者能够前瞻的那段时间。

normal.en: Unforeseeable reverses the word with un-, meaning not able to be anticipated.
normal.cn: unforeseeable 用 un- 反转词义，表示无法预料。

normal.en: Law asks whether harm was foreseeable, that is, within reasonable anticipation.
normal.cn: 法律会问损害是否可预见，也就是是否在合理预料的范围内。

abstract.en: Picture a lookout on a hill who sees the dust of a marching army long before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象山上的瞭望者，在军队到达之前很久就看见扬起的尘土。

abstract.en: Imagine a calendar whose last page is visible, marking where planning must stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，最后一页清晰可见，标出规划必须停止的地方。

abstract.en: See a judge holding a map of every harm that could have been expected.
abstract.cn: 想象法官拿着一张图，上面标出所有本可预料到的损害。

examples.en: The storm damage was foreseeable, yet nobody prepared for it.
examples.cn: 风暴造成的损失本可预见，却没有人为此做准备。

examples.en: In the foreseeable future, the town will need a new school.
examples.cn: 在可预见的未来，这座小镇将需要一所新学校。

examples.en: The company failed to warn workers of foreseeable risks.
examples.cn: 公司没有就可预见的风险提醒工人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛西额波」——仿佛「佛系」地提前看见，于是记住「可预见的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fore（在前）加 seon（看见）构成 foresee（预见），再加拉丁语 -abilis（能……的）成为 foreseeable，核心义「能提前看到」。

sensesIntro.en: Foreseeable moves from what can be anticipated at all, to what falls inside a planning horizon, and then to the legal test of reasonable anticipation.
sensesIntro.cn: foreseeable 从「原则上能预料」走到「落在规划时间范围内」，再走到法律上的「合理预见」标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lookout on high ground seeing what will reach the valley below.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在高处的瞭望者，看见即将抵达山谷的东西。

branches.en: The core sense is what the mind can know in advance.
branches.cn: 核心义是头脑能够提前知道的事。

branches.en: The time-horizon sense limits foresight to a span people can plan for.
branches.cn: 时间范围义把预见限制在人们能规划的跨度内。

branches.en: The legal sense turns anticipation into a standard of responsibility.
branches.cn: 法律义把预见变成责任标准。

branches.en: A foreseeable event is first imaginable and then placed inside a planning window.
branches.cn: 可预见的事件先是可以想象的，随后被放进规划窗口。

branches.en: Both the general and the legal sense rest on what a reasonable mind could see ahead.
branches.cn: 一般义与法律义都建立在理性头脑能够提前看见的东西上。

intro.en: Foreseeable joins a Germanic prefix and verb with a Latin suffix; its family includes foresee, foresight, and unforeseeable.
intro.cn: foreseeable 把日耳曼语的前缀与动词和拉丁语后缀结合在一起，词族包括 foresee、foresight 与 unforeseeable。

latinIntro.en: The only Latin element is the suffix -abilis, which reached English as -able through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 其中唯一的拉丁成分是后缀 -abilis，它经古法语变成英语的 -able。

items.example: Fore- opens words such as foresee and foretell.
items.exampleCN: fore- 出现在 foresee、foretell 这类词的开头。

items.meaning: to perceive with the eyes or the mind
items.example: See is the verb at the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: see 是这个词族的核心动词。

items.example: Foresee adds fore- to see.
items.exampleCN: foresee 由 fore- 加 see 构成。

items.example: Foreseeable adds -able to foresee.
items.exampleCN: foreseeable 由 foresee 加 -able 构成。

items.example: The suffix -able turns verbs into adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把动词变成形容词。

items.example: Un- negates foreseeable.
items.exampleCN: un- 否定 foreseeable。

items.example: The noun marks the legal quality of being foreseeable.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词表示法律上的可预见性。

items.example: The -er suffix names the person.
items.exampleCN: -er 后缀指人。

items.example: Foresight shares fore- but builds on sight.
items.exampleCN: foresight 共享 fore-，但以 sight 为核心。

definition_zh: 远见；先见之明；预见；深谋远虑
definition_en: the ability to see what is likely to happen and to prepare for it
core_image: 站在船头，用望远镜看见前方的暗礁
scene: 老船长凭多年经验预感到风暴将至，提前改了航线。The old captain had the foresight to change course before the storm arrived.
sceneCN: 这里「foresight」是「远见」（第 1 个义项：预判未来并提前准备的能力）；句意：老船长预感到风暴将至，提前改了航线。

derivatives.zh: 由 foresight 加 -ed 构成，义为「有远见的」
由 foresighted 加 -ness 构成，义为「远见；先见之明」
由 foresight 加 -ful 构成，义为「有远见的」

senses.title: The ability to look ahead
senses.definition: the ability to see what is likely to happen and to act in advance
senses.definitionCN: 预见可能发生之事并提前行动的能力
senses.example: She had the foresight to save money before the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 她有先见之明，在危机之前就存了钱。
senses.why: Fore- means before and sight means seeing, so foresight pictures a mind that sees events before they arrive.
senses.whyCN: fore- 表示「在前」，sight 表示「看见」，所以 foresight 描绘的是一颗在事情到来之前就看见它的头脑。

senses.title: Prudent care for the future
senses.definition: careful preparation for future needs, especially in providing for them
senses.definitionCN: 为未来的需要做周全准备，尤指提前储备
senses.example: The family showed foresight in storing grain for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人很有远见，提前存粮过冬。
senses.why: The seeing-ahead image turns into practical provision: a person acts now for a need that has not yet arrived.
senses.whyCN: 「提前看见」的意象转化为实际的储备：人在需求尚未到来时就行动。

senses.title: The front sight of a firearm
senses.definition: the sight fixed near the muzzle of a gun, used to aim at a target
senses.definitionCN: 固定在枪口附近、用于瞄准目标的准星
senses.example: He aligned the foresight with the target before firing.
senses.exampleCN: 开火前，他把前准星对准了目标。
senses.why: The literal image of seeing ahead survives in gunnery: the foresight is the sight placed at the front of the barrel.
senses.whyCN: 「向前看」的字面意象在枪械上保留下来：前准星就是装在枪管前端的瞄准具。

intro.en: Foresight is a native English compound of fore, meaning before, and sight, meaning the act of seeing.
intro.cn: foresight 是英语本族复合词，由 fore（在前）与 sight（看见）构成。

items.en: Fore means before or in front of.
items.cn: fore 意为「在……之前」或「在……前面」。

items.en: Gesihth means sight, the power of seeing.
items.cn: gesihth 意为「视觉」「看见的能力」。

items.en: Forsight names the act of looking ahead and prudent provision.
items.cn: forsight 指向前看的行为，也指周全的准备。

items.en: The spelling settles as foresight in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪时，拼写固定为 foresight。

items.en: Modern English adds the gunnery sense of a front sight.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了枪械「前准星」这一义项。

note.en: Foresight shares the fore- family with foresee and foreseeable, and it sits near forethought and prescience.
note.cn: foresight 与 foresee、foreseeable 同属 fore- 词族，意义上靠近 forethought 与 prescience。

entries.definition: to know or see something before it happens
able to be anticipated
understanding of an event only after it has happened
entries.definitionCN: 事后认识；事后聪明（与 foresight 共用 sight，但方向相反）

entries.definition: careful thought given to what may happen
knowledge of events before they happen
a deep and accurate understanding of a situation

normalIntro.en: Foresight is fore plus sight: seeing before, then turning that view into preparation.
normalIntro.cn: foresight 就是 fore 加 sight：先看见前方，再把看见的东西变成准备。

normal.en: Fore means before, and sight means seeing, so foresight is seeing ahead.
normal.cn: fore 是「在前」，sight 是「看见」，合起来就是向前看见。

normal.en: Have the foresight to act means to prepare before the need appears.
normal.cn: have the foresight to act 指在需求出现之前就做准备。

normal.en: Strategic foresight is the long-range version used in planning.
normal.cn: strategic foresight 是规划中使用的长期版本。

normal.en: Foresighted describes a person, while foresight names the quality.
normal.cn: foresighted 形容人，foresight 指这种品质本身。

normal.en: Hindsight looks back, foresight looks forward; the two share the sight element.
normal.cn: hindsight 向后看，foresight 向前看，两者共享 sight 这一成分。

abstract.en: Imagine a lookout at the top of a mast who spots a reef before the hull reaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象桅杆顶端的瞭望者，在船身触礁之前就看见暗礁。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer carrying grain into the storehouse while the sky is still clear.
abstract.cn: 想象农民在天空还很晴朗时，把粮食搬进仓房。

abstract.en: See the small sight at the muzzle of a rifle, placed there to aim forward.
abstract.cn: 想象步枪枪口上的小准星，装在那里正是为了向前瞄准。

examples.en: Her foresight saved the company from a serious loss.
examples.cn: 她的远见使公司免于重大损失。

examples.en: With foresight, the villagers stored food before the winter.
examples.cn: 村民们很有远见，入冬前就储备了食物。

examples.en: The plan shows foresight rather than luck.
examples.cn: 这项计划靠的是远见，而不是运气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛赛特」——「佛」站在前面看（sight），就是远见；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fore（在前）加 gesihth（看见）→ 中古英语 forsight → 现代英语 foresight，核心义「向前看见」。

sensesIntro.en: Foresight begins as the ability to see ahead, grows into prudent provision for the future, and keeps a literal forward-sight sense in gunnery.
sensesIntro.cn: foresight 从「向前看见」的能力出发，发展为为未来做周全准备，并在枪械领域保留「前准星」的字面义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lookout at the bow seeing the reef ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在船头的人看见前方的暗礁。

branches.en: The ability to look ahead is the central sense.
branches.cn: 向前看见的能力是核心义。

branches.en: Prudent provision turns the view into action.
branches.cn: 周全的准备把看见的东西变成行动。

branches.en: The gunnery sense keeps the literal front sight.
branches.cn: 枪械义保留字面上的前准星。

branches.en: A person with foresight both sees and prepares.
branches.cn: 有远见的人既看见又准备。

branches.en: Both senses place something at the front: provision in time and a sight in space.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把东西放在前方：时间上的预备与空间上的准星。

intro.en: Foresight is a Germanic compound; its family includes foresee, foreseeable, foresighted, and hindsight.
intro.cn: foresight 是日耳曼语复合词，词族包括 foresee、foreseeable、foresighted 与 hindsight。

latinIntro.en: Foresight has no Latin root; the word is wholly Germanic, so no Latin kin are listed.
latinIntro.cn: foresight 没有拉丁词根，整个词属于日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Fore- puts the idea of before into foresight.
items.exampleCN: fore- 把「在前」的意思放进 foresight。

items.meaning: the power or act of seeing
items.example: Sight supplies the seeing half of the word.
items.exampleCN: sight 提供这个词中「看见」的一半。

items.example: Foresight joins fore- and sight.
items.exampleCN: foresight 由 fore- 与 sight 组合而成。

items.example: The suffix -ed turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 表示这种品质。

items.example: The suffix -ful means full of.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 意为「充满……的」。

items.example: Foresee shares fore- but uses the verb see.
items.exampleCN: foresee 共享 fore-，但核心是动词 see。

items.example: Foreseeable builds on the same fore- family.
items.exampleCN: foreseeable 也属于同一个 fore- 词族。

items.example: Hindsight reverses the direction of foresight.
items.exampleCN: hindsight 把 foresight 的方向反过来。
